translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 284
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 284

sentences.zh: 【後晉紀五】 起閼逢執徐二月，盡旃蒙大荒落七月，凡一年有奇。

translations.literal: [Later Jin Records 5] Beginning in the second month of Quefeng Zhitu, ending in the seventh month of Zhanmeng Dahuangluo, in all a year and a fraction.
translations.idiomatic: [Later Jin Records 5] From the second month of the jiashen year through the seventh month of the following year—slightly more than one year in all.

sentences.zh: 齊王中開運元年（

translations.literal: First year of Kaiyun of the Later Jin ruler (
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyun 1 of Later Jin (

sentences.zh: 甲辰，公元九四四年）

translations.literal: jiachen, corresponding to the year 944 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jiachen, 944 CE)

sentences.zh: 二月，甲辰朔，命前保義節度使石贇守麻家口，前威勝節度使何重建守楊劉鎮，護聖都指揮使白再榮守馬家口，西京留守安彥威守河陽。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the first day jiachen, he ordered the former military governor of Baoyi, Shi Yun, to hold Majiakou; the former military governor of Weisheng, He Chongjian, to hold Yangliu garrison; the commander of the Imperial Guard, Bai Zairong, to hold Majiakou; and the western capital regent An Yanwei to hold Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the new moon of jiachen day, the emperor appointed the former Baoyi military governor Shi Yun to defend Majiakou, former Weisheng governor He Chongjian to hold Yangliu, Imperial Guard commander Bai Zairong to hold Majiakou again, and western capital regent An Yanwei to defend Heyang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，周儒引契丹將麻答自馬家口濟河，營於東岸，攻鄆州北津以應楊光遠。

translations.literal: Before long, Zhou Ru led the Khitan general Maduo across the river from Majiakou, encamped on the east bank, and attacked the northern ford of Yanzhou to coordinate with Yang Guangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhou Ru guided the Khitan general Maduo across at Majiakou, pitched camp on the east bank, and struck Yanzhou's northern crossing to link up with Yang Guangyuan.

sentences.zh: 麻答，契丹主之從弟也。

translations.literal: Maduo was a younger cousin of the Khitan ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Maduo was a cousin of the Khitan emperor.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，遣侍衛馬軍都指揮使、義成節度使李守貞、神武統軍皇甫遇、陳州防禦使梁漢璋、懷州刺史薛懷讓將兵萬人，緣河水陸俱進。

translations.literal: On yisi day he dispatched the commander of the palace horse guard and Yicheng military governor Li Shouzhen, Shenwu army commander Huangfu Yu, Chenzhou defense commissioner Liang Hanzhang, and Huaizhou prefect Xue Huairang with ten thousand troops to advance by land and water along the river.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day he sent palace cavalry commander and Yicheng governor Li Shouzhen, Shenwu commander Huangfu Yu, Chenzhou defender Liang Hanzhang, and Huaizhou prefect Xue Huairang with ten thousand men to press forward along the river by both land and water.

sentences.zh: 守貞，河陽；

translations.literal: Shouzhen was from Heyang;
translations.idiomatic: Li Shouzhen was a native of Heyang;

sentences.zh: 漢璋，應州；

translations.literal: Hanzhang was from Yingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hanzhang was from Yingzhou;

sentences.zh: 懷讓，太原人也。

translations.literal: Huairang was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Huairang came from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 丙午，契丹圍高行周、符彥卿及先鋒指揮使石公霸於戚城。

translations.literal: On bingwu day the Khitan besieged Gao Xingzhou, Fu Yanqing, and vanguard commander Shi Gongba at Qicheng.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day the Khitan surrounded Gao Xingzhou, Fu Yanqing, and vanguard commander Shi Gongba at Qicheng.

sentences.zh: 先是景延廣令諸將分地而守，無得相救。

translations.literal: Earlier Jing Yanguang had ordered the generals each to hold a separate sector and not to rescue one another.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jing Yanguang had ordered each general to defend his own sector and forbidden mutual relief.

sentences.zh: 行周等告急，延廣徐白帝，帝自將救之。

translations.literal: Xingzhou and the others sent urgent appeals; Yanguang slowly informed the emperor, and the emperor personally led a rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingzhou and the others cried for help, Yanguang only slowly reported to the emperor, who then led the army to relieve them in person.

sentences.zh: 契丹解去，三將泣訴救兵之緩，幾不免。

translations.literal: The Khitan lifted the siege and withdrew; the three generals wept and complained that the relief had been slow and they had barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan lifted the siege and withdrew. The three generals wept before the emperor, protesting that relief had come so late they had nearly been lost.

sentences.zh: 戊申，李守貞等至馬家口。

translations.literal: On wushen day Li Shouzhen and the others reached Majiakou.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day Li Shouzhen and his force reached Majiakou.

sentences.zh: 契丹遣步卒萬人築壘，散騎兵於其外，餘兵數萬屯河西，船數十艘渡兵，未已，晉兵薄之，契丹騎兵退走，晉兵進攻其壘，拔之。

translations.literal: The Khitan sent ten thousand foot soldiers to build a stockade, posted cavalry outside it, and stationed several tens of thousands more west of the river; several dozen boats were ferrying troops across, but before they finished the Jin troops pressed them, the Khitan cavalry fled, and the Jin troops assaulted the stockade and took it.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan put ten thousand infantry to building a camp with cavalry deployed outside, while tens of thousands more waited west of the river and dozens of boats ferried men across. Before the crossing was complete Jin troops closed in; Khitan horse fled, and the Jin stormed the camp and captured it.

sentences.zh: 契丹大敗，乘馬赴河溺死者數千人，俘斬亦數千人。

translations.literal: The Khitan suffered a great defeat; several thousand drowned riding their horses into the river, and several thousand more were captured or killed.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were routed. Thousands drowned trying to ride into the river, and thousands more were taken or slain.

sentences.zh: 河西之兵慟哭而去，由是不敢復東。

translations.literal: The troops west of the river wailed as they withdrew and thereafter did not dare march east again.
translations.idiomatic: The army west of the river withdrew in grief and did not dare advance east again.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，定難節度使李彝殷奏將兵四萬自麟州濟河，侵契丹之境。

translations.literal: On xinhai day Dingnan military governor Li Yiyin memorialized that he would lead forty thousand troops across the river from Linzhou to raid Khitan territory.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day Dingnan governor Li Yiyin reported that he would cross from Linzhou with forty thousand men to invade Khitan lands.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以彝殷為契丹西南面招討使。

translations.literal: On renzi day Li Yiyin was appointed Khitan southwest pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day Li Yiyin was made commissioner for the southwest pacification of the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 初，契丹主得貝州、博州，皆撫尉其人，或拜官賜服章。

translations.literal: At first, when the Khitan ruler took Beizhou and Bozhou, he comforted the people in each place and sometimes bestowed offices and robes of rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan emperor first seized Beizhou and Bozhou he reassured the populace and sometimes granted office and insignia of rank.

sentences.zh: 及敗於戚城及馬家口，忿恚，所得民，皆殺之，得軍士，燔炙之。

translations.literal: After defeats at Qicheng and Majiakou he was enraged; civilians he had taken were all killed, and soldiers he captured were roasted alive.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeats at Qicheng and Majiakou his rage turned murderous: civilians in his hands were slaughtered, and captured soldiers were burned alive.

sentences.zh: 由是晉人憤怒，戮力爭奮。

translations.literal: Because of this the people of Jin were furious and strove together with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Jin subjects were enraged by this and fought with united fury.

sentences.zh: 楊光遠將青州兵欲西會契丹。

translations.literal: Yang Guangyuan was leading Qingzhou troops intending to join the Khitan in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan was marching Qingzhou troops west to link up with the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 戊午，詔石贇分兵屯鄆州以備之。

translations.literal: On wuwu day an edict ordered Shi Yun to detach troops and garrison Yanzhou against him.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day the court ordered Shi Yun to detach troops and station them at Yanzhou as a precaution.

sentences.zh: 詔劉知遠將部兵自土門出恆州擊契丹，又詔會杜威、馬全節於邢州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Liu Zhiyuan to lead his division out through Tumen toward Hengzhou to strike the Khitan, and also ordered him to join Du Wei and Ma Quanjie at Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhiyuan was ordered to march from Tumen toward Hengzhou against the Khitan and to rendezvous with Du Wei and Ma Quanjie at Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 知遠引兵屯樂平不進。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan led his troops to camp at Leping and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhiyuan halted at Leping and refused to move forward.

sentences.zh: 帝居喪期年，即於宮中奏細聲女樂。

translations.literal: Though the emperor was still within the year of mourning, he already had soft-voiced female musicians perform in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Although the mourning year had not ended, the emperor already had delicate female music played within the palace.

sentences.zh: 及出師，常令左右奏三弦琵琶，和以羌笛，擊鼓歌舞，曰：「此非樂也。」

translations.literal: When he went on campaign he often had attendants play three-string pipa harmonized with Qiang flutes, beating drums and dancing, saying, "This is not music."
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he often had attendants play three-string pipa with Qiang flutes, drums, and song, remarking, "This is not pleasure."

sentences.zh: 庚申，百官表請聽樂，詔不許。

translations.literal: On gengshen day the officials memorialized asking permission to hear music; an edict refused.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day the bureaucracy petitioned to allow music; the edict refused.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，楊光遠圍棣州，刺史李瓊出兵擊敗之，光遠燒營走還青州。

translations.literal: On renxu day Yang Guangyuan besieged Dizhou; prefect Li Qiong led troops out, defeated him, and Guangyuan burned his camp and fled back to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day Yang Guangyuan besieged Dizhou. Prefect Li Qiong sallied forth, routed him, and Guangyuan burned his camp and fled to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以前威勝節度使何重建為東面馬步都部署，將兵屯鄆州。

translations.literal: On guihai day the former Weisheng military governor He Chongjian was made eastern horse-and-foot commander-in-chief and led troops to garrison Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day former Weisheng governor He Chongjian was appointed eastern commander of horse and foot and stationed at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 階、成義軍指揮使王君懷帥所部千餘人叛降蜀，請為鄉導以取階、成。

translations.literal: Wang Junhuai, commander of the Jie and Cheng righteous army, led more than a thousand of his men in revolt to surrender to Shu and offered to guide them to take Jie and Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Junhuai, commander of the Jie-Cheng righteous army, defected to Shu with over a thousand men and offered to guide an attack on Jie and Cheng.

sentences.zh: 甲子，蜀人攻階州。

translations.literal: On jiazi day the people of Shu attacked Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day Shu forces attacked Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹偽棄元城去，伏精騎於古頓丘城，以俟晉軍與恆、定之兵合而擊之。

translations.literal: The Khitan pretended to abandon Yuancheng and withdraw, but hid elite cavalry at ancient Dundunqiu to wait until Jin troops joined with the armies of Heng and Ding and then strike them.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan feigned abandonment of Yuancheng and lay in ambush with elite horse at ancient Dundunqiu, intending to strike once Jin forces merged with the Heng and Ding contingents.

sentences.zh: 鄴都留守張從恩屢奏虜已遁去；

translations.literal: Ye capital regent Zhang Cong'en repeatedly memorialized that the barbarians had already fled;
translations.idiomatic: Ye capital regent Zhang Cong'en repeatedly reported that the enemy had fled;

sentences.zh: 大軍欲進追之，會霖雨而止。

translations.literal: the main army wished to advance in pursuit but stopped because of heavy rain.
translations.idiomatic: the main army prepared to pursue but halted for torrential rain.

sentences.zh: 契丹設伏旬日，人馬饑疲。

translations.literal: The Khitan lay in ambush for ten days until men and horses were hungry and weary.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan waited in ambush for ten days until men and horses were starving and exhausted.

sentences.zh: 趙延壽曰：「晉軍悉在河上，畏我鋒銳，必不敢前，不如即其城下，四合攻之，奪其浮梁，則天下定矣。」

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou said, "The Jin armies are all along the river; they fear our sharp edge and surely will not dare advance. Better to go straight under their walls, attack from four sides, and seize their pontoon bridge—then the realm will be settled."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou said, "Jin forces are all along the river and fear our edge—they will not dare come forward. Better to strike straight at their walls from four sides and seize the pontoon bridge; then the realm is ours."

sentences.zh: 契丹主從之，三月，癸酉朔，自將兵十餘萬陳於澶州城北，東西橫掩城之兩隅，登城望之，不見其際。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler agreed. In the third month, on the new moon guiyou, he personally led more than a hundred thousand troops and drew them up north of Chuanzhou, stretching east and west to cover both corners of the wall; from atop the wall one looked out and could not see their end.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor agreed. On the third-month new moon of guiyou he personally led over a hundred thousand men and formed battle lines north of Chuanzhou, stretching east and west to flank both corners of the city. From the walls the host seemed endless.

sentences.zh: 高行周前軍在戚城之南，與契丹戰，自午至晡，互有勝負。

translations.literal: Gao Xingzhou's vanguard was south of Qicheng and fought the Khitan from noon until late afternoon with alternating victories.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xingzhou's vanguard south of Qicheng fought the Khitan from noon to dusk with neither side gaining a clear edge.

sentences.zh: 契丹主以精兵當中軍而來，帝亦出陳以待之。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler came with elite troops against the center; the emperor also went out and drew up his line to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor advanced on the center with picked troops; the Jin emperor likewise deployed to receive him.

sentences.zh: 契丹主望見晉軍之盛，謂左右曰：「楊光遠言晉兵半已餒死，今何其多也！」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler looked and saw the strength of the Jin army; he said to those beside him, "Yang Guangyuan said half the Jin soldiers had already starved to death—why are there so many now!"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the mass of Jin troops, the Khitan emperor told his attendants, "Yang Guangyuan said half the Jin army had starved—why are there so many?"

sentences.zh: 以精騎左右略陳，晉軍不動，萬弩齊發，飛矢蔽地。

translations.literal: He sent elite cavalry to probe the line left and right; the Jin army did not stir, and ten thousand crossbows fired together until flying arrows darkened the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He sent elite horse to probe both flanks. The Jin line held firm as ten thousand crossbows loosed together and arrows blotted out the ground.

sentences.zh: 契丹稍卻；

translations.literal: The Khitan fell back slightly;
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan drew back slightly;

sentences.zh: 又攻晉陳之東偏，不克。

translations.literal: then attacked the eastern flank of the Jin battle line but could not break it.
translations.idiomatic: then struck the eastern wing of the Jin line but failed to break it.

sentences.zh: 苦戰至暮，兩軍死者不可勝數。

translations.literal: They fought bitterly until evening, and the dead on both sides were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The bitter fighting lasted until nightfall; dead on both sides were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 昏後，契丹引去，營於三十里之外。

translations.literal: After dark the Khitan withdrew and encamped more than thirty li away.
translations.idiomatic: After dark the Khitan withdrew and pitched camp thirty li distant.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，契丹主帳下小校竊其馬亡來，雲契丹已傳木書，收軍北去。

translations.literal: On yihai day a junior officer under the Khitan ruler stole his horse and fled to the Jin side, reporting that the Khitan had already issued wooden tallies ordering the army to withdraw north.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day a Khitan camp orderly stole a horse and defected, reporting that wooden tallies had gone out ordering a northern withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 景延廣疑其詐，閉壁不敢追。

translations.literal: Jing Yanguang suspected a ruse, shut the walls, and did not dare pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Yanguang suspected deception, shut the gates, and would not pursue.

sentences.zh: 漢主命中書令、都元帥越王弘昌謁烈宗陵於海曲，至昌華宮，使盜殺之。

translations.literal: The Han ruler ordered chief minister and commander-in-chief Prince Yue Hongchang to visit Emperor Liezong's tomb on the seacoast; when he reached Changhua Palace, he had robbers kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Han ruler ordered chief minister and commander Prince Yue Hongchang to visit Emperor Liezong's tomb by the sea. At Changhua Palace he had assassins kill him.

sentences.zh: 契丹主自澶州北分為兩軍，一出滄、德，一出深、冀而歸。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler north of Chuanzhou divided into two armies, one exiting through Cang and De, the other through Shen and Ji, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: North of Chuanzhou the Khitan emperor split into two columns, one withdrawing through Cang and De and the other through Shen and Ji.

sentences.zh: 所過焚掠，方廣千里，民物殆盡。

translations.literal: Where they passed they burned and plundered; for a thousand li square people and goods were nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Their path was one of fire and plunder across a thousand-li square until people and goods were nearly gone.

sentences.zh: 留趙延照為貝州留後。

translations.literal: He left Zhao Yanzhao as acting prefect of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He left Zhao Yanzhao as acting Beizhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 麻答陷德州，擒刺史尹居璠。

translations.literal: Maduo took Dezhou and captured prefect Yin Jufan.
translations.idiomatic: Maduo captured Dezhou and took prefect Yin Jufan prisoner.

sentences.zh: 閩拱宸都指揮使朱文進，閣門使連重遇，既弒康宗，常懼國人之討，相與結婚以自固。

translations.literal: Zhu Wenjin, commander of the Min Archer's Guard, and Lian Chongyu, gate attendant, having assassinated Emperor Kang, constantly feared punishment by the people of the state and married their families to each other to strengthen themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wenjin, Min Archer's Guard commander, and Lian Chongyu, gate attendant, who had murdered Emperor Kang, lived in fear of popular retribution and sealed their bond with a marriage between their families.

sentences.zh: 閩主曦果於誅殺，嘗游西園，因醉殺控鶴指揮使魏從朗。

translations.literal: The Min ruler Xi was ruthless in executions; once while touring the Western Garden he killed in drunken rage Crane-Control commander Wei Conglang.
translations.idiomatic: Min ruler Xi was swift to kill. Touring the Western Garden once, he slew Crane-Control commander Wei Conglang in a drunken rage.

sentences.zh: 從朗，朱、連之黨也。

translations.literal: Conglang was a partisan of Zhu and Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Conglang had been an ally of Zhu and Lian.

sentences.zh: 又嘗酒酣誦白居易詩云：「惟有人心相對間，咫尺之情不能料。」

translations.literal: On another occasion, deep in wine, he recited a line of Bai Juyi's poetry: "Only between facing human hearts—feelings a hand-span apart cannot be foretold."
translations.idiomatic: Another time, deep in wine, he recited Bai Juyi: "Only between hearts that face each other—feelings an arm's length apart cannot be foretold."

sentences.zh: 因舉酒屬二人。

translations.literal: He then raised his cup and offered it to the two men.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his cup toward the two men.

sentences.zh: 二人起，流涕再拜，曰：「臣子事君父，安有他志！」

translations.literal: The two rose, weeping, bowed twice, and said, "As subjects serving our sovereign, how could we have any other intent!"
translations.idiomatic: They rose weeping, bowed twice, and said, "As subjects serving our lord, how could we harbor any other intent!"

sentences.zh: 曦不應。

translations.literal: Xi did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Xi made no answer.

sentences.zh: 二人大懼。

translations.literal: The two were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The two were terrified.

sentences.zh: 李后妒尚賢妃之寵，欲弒曦而立其子亞澄，使人告二人曰：「主人殊不平於二公，奈何？」

translations.literal: Empress Li, jealous of the favor shown Noble Consort Shangxian, wished to assassinate Xi and enthrone her son Yacheng; she sent someone to tell the two men, "Our lord is extremely displeased with you both—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Li, jealous of Noble Consort Shangxian, plotted to kill Xi and enthrone her son Yacheng. She sent word to the two: "The sovereign is deeply displeased with you—what will you do?"

sentences.zh: 會后父李真有疾，乙酉，曦如真第問疾。

translations.literal: When Empress Li's father Li Zhen fell ill, on yiyou day Xi went to Zhen's residence to inquire after his health.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Li's father Li Zhen fell ill, Xi visited his house on yiyou day to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 文進、重遇使拱宸馬步使錢達弒曦於馬上，召百官集朝堂，告之曰：「太祖昭武皇帝，光啟閩國，今子孫淫虐，荒墜厥緒。

translations.literal: Wenjin and Chongyu had Archer's Guard horse-and-foot commander Qian Da assassinate Xi on horseback, summoned the officials to the court hall, and announced, "Our founding Emperor Zhaowu enlightened the state of Min; now his descendants are debauched and cruel and have abandoned his legacy.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin and Chongyu had Archer's Guard commander Qian Da kill Xi on horseback, assembled the officials, and declared, "Founding Emperor Zhaowu brought Min to light; his descendants have grown licentious and cruel and cast off his legacy.

sentences.zh: 天厭王氏，宜更擇有德者立之。」

translations.literal: Heaven is weary of the house of Wang; we should choose another of virtue to establish."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has turned from the house of Wang. We must choose a man of virtue to enthrone."

sentences.zh: 眾莫敢言。

translations.literal: No one dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared speak.

sentences.zh: 重遇乃推文進升殿，被袞冕，帥群臣北面再拜稱臣。

translations.literal: Chongyu then pushed Wenjin up to the hall, clothed him in imperial robes and crown, and led the ministers to bow twice to the north and hail him as sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyu propelled Wenjin to the throne, dressed him in imperial regalia, and led the court to bow north and hail him sovereign.

sentences.zh: 文進自稱閩主，悉收王氏宗族延喜以下少長五十餘人，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Wenjin styled himself ruler of Min, gathered more than fifty members of the Wang clan from Yanchi downward, young and old, and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin took the title Min ruler, rounded up more than fifty Wang clansmen from Yanchi down, young and old alike, and executed them all.

sentences.zh: 葬閩主曦，謚曰睿文廣武明聖元德隆道大孝皇帝，廟號景宗。

translations.literal: He buried Min ruler Xi with the posthumous title Emperor Ruiwen Guangwu Mingsheng Yuande Longdao Daxiao and temple name Jingzong.
translations.idiomatic: He buried Xi with the posthumous title Emperor Ruiwen Guangwu Mingsheng Yuande Longdao Daxiao and temple name Jingzong.

sentences.zh: 以重遇總六軍。

translations.literal: He put Chongyu in overall command of the six armies.
translations.idiomatic: He placed Chongyu in command of all six armies.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書、判三司鄭元弼抗辭不屈，黜歸田裡，將奔建州，文進殺之。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites and fiscal commissioner Zheng Yuanbi spoke defiantly and would not yield; he was dismissed to his home district, was about to flee to Jianzhou, and Wenjin killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites and fiscal commissioner Zheng Yuanbi refused to submit, was dismissed to his estate, and was killed when he tried to flee to Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 文進下令，出宮人，罷營造，以反曦之政。

translations.literal: Wenjin issued orders to release palace women and halt construction projects, reversing Xi's policies.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin released palace women and halted construction, reversing Xi's policies.

sentences.zh: 殷主延政遣統軍使吳成義將兵討文進，不克。

translations.literal: Yin ruler Yanzheng sent army commander Wu Chengyi with troops to attack Wenjin but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin ruler Yanzheng sent army commander Wu Chengyi against Wenjin but failed to defeat him.

sentences.zh: 文進加樞密使鮑思潤同平章事，以羽林統軍使黃紹頗為泉州刺史，左軍使程文緯為漳州刺史。

translations.literal: Wenjin promoted privy councilor Bao Sirun to co-equal councilor of state, made Imperial Guard commander Huang Shaopo prefect of Quanzhou, and left army commander Cheng Wenwei prefect of Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin made privy councilor Bao Sirun co-equal councilor, appointed Imperial Guard commander Huang Shaopo Quanzhou prefect, and left army commander Cheng Wenwei Zhangzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 汀州刺史同安許文稹，舉郡降之。

translations.literal: Tingzhou prefect Xu Wenji of Tong'an surrendered the whole commandery to him.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhou prefect Xu Wenji of Tong'an surrendered his entire commandery.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，詔太原、恆、定兵各還本鎮。

translations.literal: On dinghai day an edict ordered the armies of Taiyuan, Heng, and Ding each to return to their home commands.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day the court ordered the Taiyuan, Heng, and Ding armies each to return home.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，馬全節攻契丹泰州，拔之。

translations.literal: On xinmao day Ma Quanjie attacked the Khitan Taizhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day Ma Quanjie attacked Khitan Taizhou and captured it.

sentences.zh: 敕天下籍鄉兵，每七戶共出兵械資一卒。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the realm to register militia; every seven households together were to supply arms and provisions for one soldier.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered a militia levy nationwide: every seven households were to equip and supply one soldier.

sentences.zh: 秦州兵救階州，出黃階嶺，敗蜀兵於西平。

translations.literal: Qinzhou troops went to relieve Jiezhou, came out through Huangjie Ridge, and defeated Shu forces at Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou relief troops crossed Huangjie Ridge and defeated Shu forces at Xiping.

sentences.zh: 漢以戶部侍郎陳偓同平章事。

translations.literal: Han appointed Ministry of Revenue vice minister Chen Wo co-equal councilor of state.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Han appointed revenue vice minister Chen Wo co-equal councilor.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁未，緣河巡檢使梁進以鄉社兵復取德州。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on dingwei day, river-patrol commissioner Liang Jin with local militia recovered Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on dingwei day, river patrol commissioner Liang Jin retook Dezhou with local militia.

sentences.zh: 己酉，命歸德節度使高行周、保義節度使王周留鎮澶州。

translations.literal: On jiyou day he ordered Guide military governor Gao Xingzhou and Baoyi military governor Wang Zhou to remain and garrison Chuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day he ordered Guide governor Gao Xingzhou and Baoyi governor Wang Zhou to remain at Chuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，帝發澶州；

translations.literal: On gengxu day the emperor set out from Chuanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day the emperor departed Chuanzhou;

sentences.zh: 甲寅，至大梁。

translations.literal: on jiayin day he reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: on jiayin day he reached Daliang.

sentences.zh: 侍衛馬步都指揮使、天平節度使、同平章事景延廣，既為上下所惡，帝亦憚其不遜難制；

translations.literal: Jing Yanguang, commander of palace horse and foot, Tianping military governor, and co-equal councilor, was already hated above and below; the emperor also feared his insubordination and difficulty in controlling him;
translations.idiomatic: Jing Yanguang, palace horse-and-foot commander, Tianping governor, and co-equal councilor, was hated by court and camp alike, and the emperor feared his insubordination;

sentences.zh: 桑維翰引其不救戚城之罪，辛酉，加延廣兼侍中，出為西京留守。

translations.literal: Sang Weihan cited his failure to rescue Qicheng; on xinyou day Yanguang was given the additional title of palace attendant and sent out as western capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Weihan cited his failure at Qicheng; on xinyou day Yanguang was made attendant and sent out as western capital regent.

sentences.zh: 以歸德節度使兼侍中高行周為侍衛馬步都指揮使。

translations.literal: Guide military governor and attendant Gao Xingzhou was made commander of palace horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: Guide governor and attendant Gao Xingzhou was made palace horse-and-foot commander.

sentences.zh: 延廣鬱鬱不得志，見契丹強盛，始憂國破身危，遂日夜縱酒。

translations.literal: Yanguang was depressed and unfulfilled; seeing the Khitan strong, he began to fear the state's ruin and his own peril, and thereafter drank day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang brooded in frustration. Seeing Khitan power rise, he feared ruin for state and self and drowned his days in wine.

sentences.zh: 朝廷因契丹入寇，國用愈竭，復遣使者三十六人分道括率民財，各封劍以授之。

translations.literal: Because of the Khitan invasion the court's resources grew ever more exhausted; it again dispatched thirty-six envoys by separate routes to levy the people's wealth, each granted a sealed sword.
translations.idiomatic: With the Khitan invasion draining the treasury, the court sent thirty-six envoys on separate routes to squeeze the people, each bearing a sealed sword of authority.

sentences.zh: 使者多從吏卒，攜鎖械、刀仗入民家，小大驚懼，求死無地。

translations.literal: The envoys mostly took clerks and soldiers with them, carrying fetters, blades, and staves into people's homes; young and old were terrified and had nowhere to turn for death or life.
translations.idiomatic: Most envoys brought clerks and soldiers armed with shackles and blades into private homes. Families great and small were terrified beyond endurance.

sentences.zh: 州縣吏復因緣為奸。

translations.literal: District and county clerks again used the opportunity for wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials seized the chance for further extortion.

sentences.zh: 河南府出緡錢二十萬，景延廣率三十七萬。

translations.literal: Henan prefecture was assessed two hundred thousand strings of cash; Jing Yanguang's quota was three hundred seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Henan prefecture was assessed two hundred thousand strings; Jing Yanguang's share was three hundred seventy thousand.

sentences.zh: 留守判官河南盧億言於延廣曰：「公位兼將相，富貴極矣。

translations.literal: Henan regent's aide Lu Yi of Henan said to Yanguang, "Your office combines general and minister; your wealth and honor are at their height.
translations.idiomatic: Regent's aide Lu Yi of Henan told Yanguang, "You hold both civil and military rank; your wealth and honor are complete.

sentences.zh: 今國家不幸，府庫空竭，不得已取於民。

translations.literal: Now the state is unfortunate and the treasury empty; there is no choice but to take from the people.
translations.idiomatic: The state is in distress and the treasury bare—we must take from the people.

sentences.zh: 公何忍復因而求利，為子孫之累乎！」

translations.literal: How can you bear to seek profit on top of that and burden your descendants!"
translations.idiomatic: How can you profit from this on top of that and burden your descendants?"

sentences.zh: 延廣慚而止。

translations.literal: Yanguang was ashamed and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Yanguang desisted.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔以楊光遠叛，命兗州修守備。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Yang Guangyuan had rebelled, an edict ordered Yanzhou to repair its defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Yang Guangyuan's rebellion, Yanzhou had been ordered to strengthen its defenses.

sentences.zh: 泰寧節度使安審信，以治樓堞為名，率民財以實私藏。

translations.literal: Taining military governor An Shenxin, famous for repairing battlements, drained the people's wealth to fill his private stores.
translations.idiomatic: Taining governor An Shenxin, renowned for repairing walls and towers, squeezed the people to swell his private coffers.

sentences.zh: 大理卿張仁願為括率使，至兗州，賦緡錢十萬。

translations.literal: Chief justice Zhang Renyuan served as levy commissioner; arriving at Yanzhou, he assessed one hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Chief justice Zhang Renyuan came as levy commissioner and assessed Yanzhou one hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 值審信不在，拘其守藏吏，指取錢一囷，已滿其數。

translations.literal: Shenxin was away; he detained the treasury clerk and, pointing, took one granary of cash, which already met the quota.
translations.idiomatic: With Shenxin absent, he seized the treasury clerk and, at a gesture, took one full granary of coin—already meeting the levy.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，命侍衛馬步軍都虞候、泰寧節度使李守貞將步騎二萬討楊光遠於青州，又遣神武統軍洛陽潘環及張彥澤等將兵屯澶州，以備契丹。

translations.literal: On wuyin day he ordered palace horse-and-foot deputy commander and Taining military governor Li Shouzhen to lead twenty thousand infantry and cavalry against Yang Guangyuan at Qingzhou, and also sent Shenwu commander Pan Huan of Luoyang and Zhang Yanzhe and others to garrison troops at Chuanzhou against the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day Li Shouzhen, palace deputy commander and Taining governor, was sent with twenty thousand horse and foot against Yang Guangyuan at Qingzhou. Pan Huan of Luoyang, Zhang Yanzhe, and others were posted at Chuanzhou to guard against the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 契丹遣兵救青州，齊州防禦使堂陽薛可言邀擊，敗之。

translations.literal: The Khitan sent troops to relieve Qingzhou; Qizhou defense commissioner Xue Keyan of Tangyang intercepted and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan relief troops for Qingzhou were intercepted and beaten by Qizhou defender Xue Keyan of Tangyang.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，詔諸州所籍鄉兵，號武定軍，凡得七萬餘人。

translations.literal: On bingxu day an edict named the registered militia of the prefectures the Wuding Army, totaling more than seventy thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day registered militia nationwide were organized as the Wuding Army—over seventy thousand men.

sentences.zh: 時兵荒之餘，復有此擾，民不聊生。

translations.literal: In the aftermath of war and famine this new burden came again, and the people could scarcely live.
translations.idiomatic: After war and famine, this fresh levy left the people barely able to survive.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，鄴都留守張從恩上言：「趙延照雖據貝州，麾下兵皆久客思歸，宜速進軍攻之。」

translations.literal: On dinghai day Ye capital regent Zhang Cong'en memorialized, "Although Zhao Yanzhao holds Beizhou, the troops under him are long away from home and yearn to return; we should advance quickly and attack."
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day Zhang Cong'en reported, "Zhao Yanzhao holds Beizhou, but his troops are homesick after long service—we should strike at once."

sentences.zh: 詔以從恩為貝州行營都部署，督諸將擊之。

translations.literal: An edict made Cong'en overall commander of the Beizhou field camp and ordered the generals to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Cong'en was made overall commander of the Beizhou campaign and ordered to press the attack.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，從恩奏趙延照縱火大掠，棄城而遁，屯於瀛、莫，阻水自固。

translations.literal: On xinmao day Cong'en reported that Zhao Yanzhao set fires and plundered heavily, abandoned the city and fled, and encamped at Ying and Mo, using the water as a barrier to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day Cong'en reported that Yanzhao burned and looted, fled the city, and entrenched between Ying and Mo behind the waterways.

sentences.zh: 朱文進遣使如唐，唐主囚其使，將伐之，會天暑、疾疫而止。

translations.literal: Zhu Wenjin sent envoys to Tang; the Tang ruler imprisoned them and was about to attack, but stopped because of summer heat and epidemic.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wenjin sent envoys to Tang; the Tang emperor imprisoned them and prepared to invade, but summer heat and plague halted the campaign.

sentences.zh: 六月，辛酉，官軍拔淄州，斬其刺史劉翰。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on xinyou day, government troops took Zizhou and executed its prefect Liu Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinyou day, imperial forces captured Zizhou and executed prefect Liu Han.

sentences.zh: 太尉、侍中馮道雖為首相，依違兩可，無所操決。

translations.literal: Grand preceptor and palace attendant Feng Dao, though chief minister, wavered between alternatives and made no decisive judgments.
translations.idiomatic: Though chief minister, Grand Preceptor Feng Dao sat on every fence and decided nothing.

sentences.zh: 或謂帝曰：「馮道，承平之良相；

translations.literal: Someone told the emperor, "Feng Dao is a fine minister for peaceful times;
translations.idiomatic: Someone told the emperor, "Feng Dao is a fine minister for peaceful times;

sentences.zh: 今艱難之際，譬如使禪僧飛鷹耳。」

translations.literal: in this time of hardship it is like asking a Chan monk to fly a hawk."
translations.idiomatic: in crisis he is like asking a Chan monk to fly a hawk."

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以道為匡國節度使，兼侍中。

translations.literal: On guimao day Dao was made Kuangguo military governor with the additional title of palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day Feng Dao was sent out as Kuangguo governor, retaining the title of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，漢主幽齊王弘弼於私第。

translations.literal: On yisi day the Han ruler confined Prince Qi Hongbi in a private residence.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day the Southern Han ruler confined Prince Qi Hongbi to house arrest.

sentences.zh: 或謂帝曰：「陛下欲御北狄，安天下，非桑維翰不可。」

translations.literal: Someone told the emperor, "If Your Majesty wishes to control the northern barbarians and settle the realm, no one but Sang Weihan will do."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told the emperor, "To master the northern barbarians and settle the realm, you need Sang Weihan."

sentences.zh: 丙午，復置樞密院，以維翰為中書令兼樞密使，事無大小，悉以委之。

translations.literal: On bingwu day the Bureau of Military Affairs was restored; Weihan was made chief minister and privy commissioner, and matters great and small were all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day the privy council was restored. Weihan became chief minister and privy commissioner with full authority over great and small affairs.

sentences.zh: 數月之間，朝廷差治。

translations.literal: Within a few months the court was somewhat in order.
translations.idiomatic: Within months the court regained a measure of order.

sentences.zh: 滑州河決，浸汴、曹、單、濮、鄆五州之境，環梁山合於汶。

translations.literal: The Yellow River burst its banks at Huazhou, flooding the territories of Bian, Cao, Shan, Pu, and Yan; waters circled Liangshan and joined the Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The river broke at Huazhou and inundated Bian, Cao, Shan, Pu, and Yan, circling Liangshan to merge with the Wen.

sentences.zh: 詔大發數道丁夫塞之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered corvée labor from several circuits to block it.
translations.idiomatic: The court drafted laborers from several circuits to seal the breach.

sentences.zh: 既塞，帝欲刻碑紀其事。

translations.literal: After it was sealed, the emperor wished to carve a stele to record the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Once the breach was closed, the emperor wished to erect a commemorative stele.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人楊昭儉諫曰：「陛下刻石紀功，不若降哀痛之詔；

translations.literal: Palace drafting officer Yang Zhaojian remonstrated, "Your Majesty, to carve stone recording merit is not as good as issuing an edict of grief and remorse;
translations.idiomatic: Drafting officer Yang Zhaojian urged, "A stele of triumph is less fitting than an edict of grief and repentance;

sentences.zh: 染翰頌美，不若頒罪己之文。」

translations.literal: to take brush and praise is not as good as promulgating a text of self-blame."
translations.idiomatic: praise in ink is less fitting than a proclamation of self-reproach."

sentences.zh: 帝善其言而止。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the advice and abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖割北邊之地以賂契丹，由是府州刺史折從遠亦北屬。

translations.literal: At first, because Gaozu had ceded northern borderlands to bribe the Khitan, Fuzhou prefect Zhe Congyuan also came under northern rule.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu ceded the northern frontier to the Khitan, Fuzhou prefect Zhe Congyuan fell under Khitan sway as well.

sentences.zh: 契丹欲盡徙河西之民以實遼東，州人大恐，從遠因保險拒之。

translations.literal: The Khitan wished to move all the people west of the river to populate Liaodong; the people of the prefecture were greatly afraid, and Congyuan held the defiles and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan planned to relocate all inhabitants west of the river to fill Liaodong, the populace panicked and Congyuan held the passes in resistance.

sentences.zh: 及帝與契丹絕，遣使諭從遠使攻契丹。

translations.literal: When the emperor broke with the Khitan, he sent envoys to instruct Congyuan to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: After the break with the Khitan, envoys urged Congyuan to strike them.

sentences.zh: 從遠引兵深入，拔十餘寨。

translations.literal: Congyuan led troops deep in and captured more than ten stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Congyuan marched deep into Khitan territory and took more than ten camps.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以從遠為府州團練使。

translations.literal: On wuwu day Congyuan was made regimental commissioner of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day Zhe Congyuan was appointed regimental commissioner of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 從遠，雲州人也。

translations.literal: Congyuan was a man of Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe Congyuan was a native of Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲子，復置翰林學士。

translations.literal: On jiazi day Hanlin academicians were restored.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day the Hanlin Academy posts were restored.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以右散騎常侍李慎儀為兵部侍郎、翰林學士承旨，都官郎中劉溫叟、金部郎中、知制誥武強徐台符、禮部郎中李澣、主客員外郎宗城范質，皆為學士。

translations.literal: On wuchen day right attendant cavalier Li Shenyi was made vice minister of war and Hanlin academician recipient; bureau directors Liu Wensou, Xu Taifu of Wuqiang, Li Huan, and Fan Zhi of Zongcheng were all made academicians.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day Li Shenyi became vice minister of war and chief Hanlin academician; Liu Wensou, Xu Taifu, Li Huan, and Fan Zhi were appointed academicians.

sentences.zh: 溫叟，岳之子也。

translations.literal: Wensou was the son of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wensou was the son of Liu Yue.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛未朔，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the new moon xinwei, a general amnesty was declared and the era name changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the xinwei new moon, the court proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以太子太傅劉昫為司空兼門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On jichou day Grand Mentor Liu Xu was made minister of works with concurrent post as vice director of the Secretariat and co-equal councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day Grand Mentor Liu Xu was made minister of works and co-equal councilor.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛丑朔，以河東節度使劉知遠為北面行營都統，順國節度使杜威為都招討使，督十三節度以備契丹。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the new moon xinchou, Hedong military governor Liu Zhiyuan was made northern campaign commander-in-chief and Shunguo military governor Du Wei grand pacification commissioner, supervising thirteen commands against the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth-month xinchou new moon, Hedong governor Liu Zhiyuan was made northern commander-in-chief and Shunguo governor Du Wei grand pacification commissioner over thirteen circuits against the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 桑維翰兩秉朝政，出楊光遠、景延廣於外，至是一制指揮，節度使十五人無敢違者，時人服其膽略。

translations.literal: Sang Weihan had twice held court power and sent Yang Guangyuan and Jing Yanguang abroad; now with one order he commanded, and none of fifteen military governors dared disobey—men of the time admired his daring and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Having twice held the reins of government and banished rivals abroad, Weihan now commanded fifteen governors with a single order. Contemporaries admired his nerve and grasp.

sentences.zh: 朔方節度使馮暉上章自陳未老可用，而制書見遺。

translations.literal: Shuofang military governor Feng Hui memorialized that he was not yet old and could still serve, yet the appointment edict passed him over.
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang governor Feng Hui protested that he was still fit for service though the appointment edict had omitted him.

sentences.zh: 維翰詔禁直學士使為答詔曰：「非制書勿忘，實以朔方重地，非卿無以彈壓。

translations.literal: Weihan ordered a duty academician to draft the reply: "It is not that the edict forgot you; Shuofang is a vital region and none but you can hold it down.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan had a duty academician draft the reply: "The edict did not forget you—Shuofang is vital and only you can hold it.

sentences.zh: 比欲移卿內地，受代亦須奇才。」

translations.literal: We had wished to move you inland, but your replacement also requires a rare talent."
translations.idiomatic: We wished to recall you inland, but your replacement must be a man of rare ability."

sentences.zh: 暉得詔，甚喜。

translations.literal: Hui received the edict and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Hui was greatly pleased by the reply.

sentences.zh: 時軍國多事，百司及使者咨請輻水奏，維翰隨事裁決，初若不經思慮，人疑其疏略；

translations.literal: With military and state affairs pressing, requests from all offices and envoys poured in; Weihan decided each on the spot, at first seeming unconsidered so that people suspected carelessness;
translations.idiomatic: With war pressing, memorials from every office and envoy flooded in. Weihan ruled on each at once, seeming at first cursory;

sentences.zh: 退而熟議之，亦終不能易也。

translations.literal: yet when they deliberated afterward they could never change his decisions.
translations.idiomatic: yet on later reflection none could improve his judgments.

sentences.zh: 然為相頗任愛憎，一飯之恩、睚眥之怨必報，人亦以此少之。

translations.literal: Yet as minister he indulged likes and dislikes, repaying a meal's kindness or the grudge of a sidelong glance—people therefore thought less of him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as minister he indulged personal likes and dislikes, repaying the smallest favor or slight—many faulted him for it.

sentences.zh: 契丹之入寇也，帝再命劉知遠會兵山東，皆後期不至。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded, the emperor twice ordered Liu Zhiyuan to join forces in Shandong, but both times he arrived late.
translations.idiomatic: During the Khitan invasions the emperor twice ordered Liu Zhiyuan to join forces in Shandong; both times he arrived late.

sentences.zh: 帝疑之，謂所親曰：「太原殊不助朕，必有異圖。

translations.literal: The emperor grew suspicious and told those close to him, "Taiyuan is not helping me at all—he must have other designs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew suspicious and told intimates, "Taiyuan gives me no help—he must harbor other designs.

sentences.zh: 果有分，何不速為之！」

translations.literal: If he truly has a share of destiny, why does he not act quickly!"
translations.idiomatic: If he means to claim the throne, why does he not act at once!"

sentences.zh: 至是雖為都統，而實無臨制之權，密謀大計，皆不得預。

translations.literal: Now though he was commander-in-chief, he in fact had no power of field command; he could not join in secret grand plans.
translations.idiomatic: Though named commander-in-chief, he had no real authority over the campaign and was shut out of secret strategy.

sentences.zh: 知遠亦自知見疏，但慎事自守而已。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan also knew he was distanced and could only guard himself carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan knew he was distrusted and kept cautiously to himself.

sentences.zh: 郭威見知遠有憂色，謂知遠曰：「河東山河險固，風俗尚武，士多戰馬，靜則勤稼穡，動則習軍旅，此霸王之資也，何憂乎！」

translations.literal: Guo Wei saw Zhiyuan's worried look and said to him, "Hedong's mountains and rivers are strong, its customs honor war, its gentlemen have many war-horses; in peace they till diligently, in motion they drill as soldiers—this is capital for hegemony. Why worry!"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Zhiyuan's worry, Guo Wei said, "Hedong's terrain is strong, its people warlike, its gentry well mounted. In peace they farm; in war they fight. That is capital for empire—why worry?"

sentences.zh: 朱文進自稱威武留後，權知閩國事，遣使奉表稱籓於晉。

translations.literal: Zhu Wenjin styled himself acting Weiwu regent and provisional ruler of Min affairs, and sent envoys with a memorial declaring himself vassal to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wenjin styled himself acting Weiwu regent, claimed authority over Min, and sent envoys submitting to Jin as vassal.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以文進為威武節度使，知閩國事。

translations.literal: On guichou day Wenjin was made Weiwu military governor with charge of Min affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day Zhu Wenjin was appointed Weiwu governor with authority over Min.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，置鎮寧軍於澶州，以濮州隸焉。

translations.literal: On guihai day Zhenning Army was established at Chuanzhou, with Puzhou placed under it.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day the Zhenning command was established at Chuanzhou with Puzhou subordinated to it.

sentences.zh: 初，吳濠州刺史劉金卒，子仁規代之；

translations.literal: At first, Wu's Haozhou prefect Liu Jin died and his son Rengui succeeded him;
translations.idiomatic: When Wu's Haozhou prefect Liu Jin died, his son Rengui succeeded him;

sentences.zh: 仁規卒，子崇俊代之。

translations.literal: when Rengui died, his son Chongjun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: when Rengui died, his son Chongjun took the post.

sentences.zh: 唐烈祖置定遠軍於濠州，以崇俊為節度使。

translations.literal: Tang's Emperor Liezu established Dingyuan Army at Haozhou and made Chongjun its military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Tang's Liezu emperor established the Dingyuan command at Haozhou and made Chongjun its governor.

sentences.zh: 會清淮節度使姚景卒，崇俊厚賂權要，求兼領壽州。

translations.literal: When Qinghuai military governor Yao Jing died, Chongjun bribed powerful men heavily to seek concurrent charge of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinghuai governor Yao Jing died, Chongjun bribed court power brokers to add Shouzhou to his command.

sentences.zh: 唐主陽為不知其意，徙崇俊為清淮節度使，以楚州刺史劉彥貞為濠州觀察使，馳往代之；

translations.literal: The Tang ruler pretended not to know his intent, transferred Chongjun to Qinghuai, and made Chuzhou prefect Liu Yanzhen Haozhou observation commissioner, rushing him to replace him;
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor feigned ignorance, moved Chongjun to Qinghuai, and rushed Chuzhou prefect Liu Yanzhen to Haozhou as observation commissioner;

sentences.zh: 崇俊悔之。

translations.literal: Chongjun regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjun bitterly regretted his miscalculation.

sentences.zh: 彥貞，信之子也。

translations.literal: Yanzhen was the son of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanzhen was the son of Liu Xin.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚午朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the new moon gengwu, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth-month gengwu new moon there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 丙子，契丹寇遂城、樂壽，深州刺史康彥進擊卻之。

translations.literal: On bingzi day the Khitan raided Suicheng and Leshou; Shenzhou prefect Kang Yanjin attacked and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day the Khitan raided Suicheng and Leshou; Shenzhou prefect Kang Yanjin repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙午，漢主毒殺鎮王弘澤於邕州。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on bingwu day, the Han ruler poisoned Prince Zhen Hongze at Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on bingwu day, the Southern Han ruler poisoned Prince Zhen Hongze at Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 殷主延政遣其將陳敬佺以兵三千屯尤溪及古田，盧進以兵二千屯長溪。

translations.literal: Yin ruler Yanzheng sent his general Chen Jingxian with three thousand troops to garrison Youxi and Gutian, and Lu Jin with two thousand at Changxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yin ruler Yanzheng posted Chen Jingxian with three thousand men at Youxi and Gutian, and Lu Jin with two thousand at Changxi.

sentences.zh: 泉州散員指揮使桃林留從效謂同列王忠順、董思安、張漢思曰：「朱文進屠滅王氏，遣腹心分據諸州。

translations.literal: Quanzhou irregular commander Liu Congxiao of Taolin said to his comrades Wang Zhongshun, Dong Si'an, and Zhang Hansi, "Zhu Wenjin slaughtered the house of Wang and sent trusted men to hold the prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhou irregular commander Liu Congxiao of Taolin told Wang Zhongshun, Dong Si'an, and Zhang Hansi, "Zhu Wenjin exterminated the Wang clan and posted his men across the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 吾屬世受王氏恩，而交臂事賊，一旦富沙王克福州，吾屬死有餘愧！」

translations.literal: We have received the Wang family's grace for generations, yet we fold our arms and serve the traitor—once the Prince of Fusha takes Fuzhou, death will not erase our shame!"
translations.idiomatic: We owe the Wangs generations of grace yet serve this traitor with folded arms. When the Prince of Fusha takes Fuzhou, death will not erase our shame!"

sentences.zh: 眾以為然。

translations.literal: All agreed.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，從效等各引軍中所善壯士，夜飲於從效之家，從效給之曰：「富沙王已平福州，密旨令吾屬討黃紹頗。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Congxiao and the others each led stalwart soldiers they favored in the army to drink at night at Congxiao's home; Congxiao deceived them, saying, "The Prince of Fusha has already pacified Fuzhou and secretly ordered us to punish Huang Shaopo.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Congxiao gathered trusted soldiers for a night feast and lied, "The Prince of Fusha has taken Fuzhou and secretly orders us to kill Huang Shaopo.

sentences.zh: 吾觀諸君狀貌，皆非久處貧賤者。

translations.literal: I see by your bearing that none of you are men to remain long in poverty.
translations.idiomatic: By your bearing, none of you are meant for poverty.

sentences.zh: 從吾言，富貴可圖；

translations.literal: Follow my word and wealth and honor can be sought;
translations.idiomatic: Follow me and fortune is yours;

sentences.zh: 不然，禍且至矣。」

translations.literal: otherwise disaster will soon come."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise ruin follows."

sentences.zh: 眾皆踴躍，操白梃，逾垣而入，執紹頗，斬之。

translations.literal: All leapt up eagerly, took white clubs, climbed the wall and entered, seized Shaopo, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: They leapt up, seized white clubs, scaled the wall, seized Shaopo, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 從效持州印詣王繼勳第，請主軍府。

translations.literal: Congxiao took the prefectural seal and went to Wang Jixun's residence, asking him to head the military government.
translations.idiomatic: Congxiao took the prefectural seal to Wang Jixun's house and asked him to head the command.

sentences.zh: 從效自稱平賊統軍使，函紹頗首，遣副兵馬使臨淮陳洪進繼詣建州。

translations.literal: Congxiao styled himself pacification commander for suppressing rebels, boxed Shaopo's head, and sent deputy horse commissioner Chen Hongjin of Linhuai on to Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Congxiao styled himself pacification commander, sent Shaopo's head in a box, and dispatched Chen Hongjin of Linhuai to Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪進至尤溪，福州戍兵數千遮道。

translations.literal: Hongjin reached Youxi; several thousand Fuzhou garrison troops blocked the road.
translations.idiomatic: At Youxi several thousand Fuzhou garrison troops blocked Chen Hongjin's path.

sentences.zh: 洪進紿之曰：「義師已誅朱福州，吾倍道嗣君於建州，爾輩尚守此何為乎？」

translations.literal: Hongjin deceived them, saying, "The righteous army has already executed Zhu of Fuzhou; I am hurrying to Jianzhou to attend the ruler—why do you still hold this place?"
translations.idiomatic: Hongjin deceived them: "The loyal army has killed Zhu Wenjin. I hurry to attend our lord at Jianzhou—why do you still hold this post?"

sentences.zh: 以紹頗首示之，眾遂潰，大將數人從洪進詣建州。

translations.literal: He showed them Shaopo's head; the troops dispersed, and several senior officers followed Hongjin to Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He showed Shaopo's head; the troops dispersed, and several officers followed him to Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 延政以繼勳為侍中、泉州刺史，從效、忠順、思安、洪進皆為都指揮使。

translations.literal: Yanzheng made Jixun palace attendant and Quanzhou prefect; Congxiao, Zhongshun, Si'an, and Hongjin were all made commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzheng made Jixun attendant and Quanzhou prefect; Congxiao, Zhongshun, Si'an, and Hongjin were made commanders.

sentences.zh: 漳州將程謨聞之，立殺刺史程文緯，立王繼成權州事。

translations.literal: Zhangzhou general Cheng Mo heard of it, immediately killed prefect Cheng Wenwei, and installed Wang Jicheng to manage prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the news, Zhangzhou general Cheng Mo killed prefect Cheng Wenwei and installed Wang Jicheng as acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 繼勳、繼成，皆延政之從子也，朱文進之滅王氏，二人以疏遠獲全。

translations.literal: Jixun and Jicheng were both Yanzheng's nephews; when Zhu Wenjin destroyed the Wang house, the two survived because they were distant kin.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun and Jicheng were Yanzheng's nephews; as distant kin they alone survived Zhu Wenjin's purge of the Wang clan.

sentences.zh: 汀州刺史許文稹奉表請降於殷。

translations.literal: Tingzhou prefect Xu Wenji submitted a memorial requesting surrender to Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhou prefect Xu Wenji submitted his surrender to Yin.

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸丑，加朱文進同平章事，封閩國王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on guichou day, Zhu Wenjin was given the additional title of co-equal councilor and enfeoffed as king of Min.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on guichou day, Zhu Wenjin was made co-equal councilor and enfeoffed as king of Min.

sentences.zh: 李守貞圍青州經時，城中食盡，餓死者太半。

translations.literal: Li Shouzhen had besieged Qingzhou for a long time; food in the city was exhausted and more than half died of hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shouzhen's long siege of Qingzhou exhausted the city's food; more than half the population starved.

sentences.zh: 契丹援兵不至，楊光遠遙稽首於契丹曰：「皇帝，皇帝，誤光遠矣！」

translations.literal: Khitan relief did not arrive; Yang Guangyuan bowed from afar toward the Khitan, saying, "Emperor, Emperor—you have misled Guangyuan!"
translations.idiomatic: With no Khitan relief, Yang Guangyuan kowtowed toward the north crying, "Emperor, Emperor—you have misled me!"

sentences.zh: 其子承勳、承祚、承信勸光遠降，冀全其族。

translations.literal: His sons Chengxun, Chengzuo, and Chengxin urged Guangyuan to surrender, hoping to preserve the clan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Chengxun, Chengzuo, and Chengxin urged surrender to save the family.

sentences.zh: 光遠不許，曰：「吾昔在代北，嘗以紙錢祭天池而沈，人皆言當為天子，姑待之。」

translations.literal: Guangyuan refused, saying, "Long ago in the northern Dai region I once offered paper money at Heaven Pool and sank it; everyone said I would become Son of Heaven—let us wait."
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan refused: "In the northern frontier I once offered paper money at Heaven Pool and cast it in—the omens said I would be emperor. We must wait."

sentences.zh: 丁巳，承勳斬勸光遠反者節度判官丘濤等，送其首於守貞，縱火大噪，劫其父出居私第，上表待罪，開城納官軍。

translations.literal: On dingsi day Chengxun killed those urging Guangyuan to rebel, including military aide Qiu Tao, sent their heads to Shouzhen, set fires and raised a great clamor, seized his father to a private residence, submitted a memorial awaiting punishment, and opened the city to admit government troops.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi day Chengxun killed Guangyuan's advisers including aide Qiu Tao, sent their heads to Shouzhen, raised a tumult, moved his father to a private house, submitted a plea for mercy, and opened the gates to imperial troops.

sentences.zh: 朱文進聞黃紹頗死，大懼，以重賞募兵二萬，遣統軍使林守諒、內客省使李廷鍔將之攻泉州，鉦鼓相聞五百里。

translations.literal: Zhu Wenjin heard that Huang Shaopo was dead and was greatly afraid; with rich rewards he recruited twenty thousand troops and sent army commander Lin Shouliang and inner palace envoy Li Ting'e to attack Quanzhou—the sound of gongs and drums was heard for five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Shaopo's death, Zhu Wenjin in terror recruited twenty thousand men and sent Lin Shouliang and Li Ting'e against Quanzhou—the din of drums carried five hundred li.

sentences.zh: 殷主延政遣大將軍杜進將兵二萬救泉州，留從效開門與福州兵戰，大破之，斬守諒，執廷鍔。

translations.literal: Yin ruler Yanzheng sent grand general Du Jin with twenty thousand troops to relieve Quanzhou; Congxiao opened the gates and fought Fuzhou troops, routing them greatly, beheading Shouliang and capturing Ting'e.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzheng sent Du Jin with twenty thousand relief troops. Congxiao sallied forth, routed the Fuzhou army, killed Shouliang, and captured Ting'e.

sentences.zh: 延政遣統軍使吳成義帥戰艦千艘攻福州，朱文進遣子弟為質於吳越以求救。

translations.literal: Yanzheng sent army commander Wu Chengyi with a thousand warships to attack Fuzhou; Zhu Wenjin sent his sons and younger brothers as hostages to Wuyue to seek rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzheng sent Wu Chengyi with a thousand warships against Fuzhou. Zhu Wenjin sent kinsmen as hostages to Wuyue begging for aid.

sentences.zh: 初，唐翰林待詔臧循，與樞密副使查文徽同鄉里，循常為賈人，習福建山川，為文徽畫取建州之策。

translations.literal: At first, Tang Hanlin awaiting-edict Zang Xun was from the same home district as privy deputy commissioner Zha Wenhui; Xun had often been a merchant and knew Fujian's mountains and rivers, and drew up for Wenhui a plan to take Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Hanlin attendant Zang Xun, a townsman of privy deputy Zha Wenhui, had been a merchant and knew Fujian's terrain. He drafted a plan to seize Jianzhou for Wenhui.

sentences.zh: 文徽表請用兵擊王延政，國人多以為不可。

translations.literal: Wenhui memorialized requesting troops to attack Wang Yanzheng; many in the state thought it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhui petitioned to attack Wang Yanzheng; most at court thought it unwise.

sentences.zh: 唐主以文徽為江西安撫使，循行境上，覘其可否；

translations.literal: The Tang ruler made Wenhui Jiangxi pacification commissioner and had Xun tour the border to observe whether it was feasible;
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor made Wenhui Jiangxi pacification commissioner and sent Xun to scout the border;

sentences.zh: 文徽至信州，奏言攻之必克。

translations.literal: when Wenhui reached Xinzhou he memorialized that an attack would surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: reaching Xinzhou, Wenhui reported that attack was certain to succeed.

sentences.zh: 唐主以洪州營屯都虞候邊鎬為行營招討諸軍都虞候，將兵從文徽伐殷。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler made Hongzhou camp deputy commander Bian Hao grand deputy of the field pacification army and led troops following Wenhui to attack Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor appointed Hongzhou deputy Bian Hao to command the expedition following Wenhui against Yin.

sentences.zh: 文徽自建陽進屯蓋竹，聞漳、泉、汀三州皆隆於殷，殷將張漢真自鏞州將兵八千將至，文徽懼，退保建陽。

translations.literal: Wenhui advanced from Jianyang to camp at Gaizhu; hearing that Zhang, Quan, and Ting had all submitted to Yin and that Yin general Zhang Hanzhen was bringing eight thousand troops from Yongzhou, Wenhui was afraid and withdrew to hold Jianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhui advanced from Jianyang to Gaizhu, learned that Zhang, Quan, and Ting had submitted to Yin and that Zhang Hanzhen was marching eight thousand men from Yongzhou, and retreated to Jianyang in fear.

sentences.zh: 臧循屯邵武，邵武民導殷兵襲破循軍，執循送建州斬之。

translations.literal: Zang Xun encamped at Shaowu; Shaowu people guided Yin troops to surprise and break Xun's army, seized Xun, and sent him to Jianzhou for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Xun camped at Shaowu. Locals guided Yin troops to surprise his force, capture him, and send him to Jianzhou for execution.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以楊光遠罪大，而諸子歸命，難於顯誅，命李守貞以便宜從事。

translations.literal: The court, because Yang Guangyuan's crimes were great, yet his sons had submitted, found it difficult to execute him openly, and ordered Li Shouzhen to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yang Guangyuan's crimes were grave but his sons had surrendered, the court found it awkward to punish him openly and ordered Li Shouzhen to deal with the matter as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 閏月，癸酉，守貞入青州，遣人拉殺光遠於別第，以病死聞。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on guiyou, Shouzhen entered Qingzhou; he sent men to drag Guangyuan out and kill him at a separate residence, and it was announced that he had died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on guiyou (day 10), Li Shouzhen entered Qingzhou and had Yang Guangyuan dragged from his private residence and killed; the court was told he had died of illness.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，起復楊承勳，除汝州防禦使。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Yang Chengxun was recalled from mourning and appointed Defender of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu (day 23), Yang Chengxun was recalled from mourning and made military commissioner of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 殷吳成義聞有唐兵，詐使人告福州吏民曰：「唐助我討賊臣，大兵今至矣。」

translations.literal: Yin Wu Chengyi, hearing that Tang troops were present, falsely sent someone to tell the officials and people of Fuzhou, saying: "Tang is aiding us in punishing the rebel ministers; the great army has now arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Wu Chengyi heard that Tang forces were in the field, he sent a false messenger to tell Fuzhou's officials and people: "Tang is helping us punish the rebel ministers—the main army has arrived."

sentences.zh: 福人益懼。

translations.literal: (close of speech.) The people of Fu grew all the more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fuzhou grew even more afraid.

sentences.zh: 乙未，朱文進遣同平章事李光准等奉國寶於殷。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Zhu Wenjin sent his fellow chief councilors Li Guangzhun and others to present the national treasures to Yin.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei (day 32), Zhu Wenjin sent fellow chief councilor Li Guangzhun and others to deliver the state regalia to Yin.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，福州南廊承旨林仁翰謂其徒曰：「吾曹世事王氏，今受制賊臣，富沙王至，何面見之！」

translations.literal: On dingyou, Lin Renhan, Director of the Southern Colonnade at Fuzhou, said to his followers: "We have served the Wang house through the generations; now we are controlled by rebel ministers. When the Prince of Fusha arrives, with what face shall we meet him!
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou (day 34), Fuzhou's Director of the Southern Colonnade, Lin Renhan, told his men: "We have served the Wang house for generations, yet now we are held captive by rebel ministers. When the Prince of Fusha comes, how can we face him?"

sentences.zh: 帥其徒三十人被甲趣連重遇第，重遇方嚴兵自衛，三十人者望之，稍稍遁去。

translations.literal: (close of speech.) He led thirty followers in armor and hurried to Lian Chongyu's residence; Chongyu was just then drilling his troops to defend himself, and when the thirty men saw them, they gradually slipped away.
translations.idiomatic: He led thirty armored followers to Lian Chongyu's mansion. Chongyu was drilling troops for his own defense; at the sight of them, the thirty men gradually melted away.

sentences.zh: 仁翰執槊直前刺重遇，殺之，斬其首以示眾曰：「富沙王且至，汝輩族矣！

translations.literal: Renhan seized a spear, went straight forward, and stabbed Chongyu, killing him; he cut off his head and showed it to the crowd, saying: "The Prince of Fusha is about to arrive—you will all be exterminated!
translations.idiomatic: Renhan took a spear, charged straight at Chongyu, and killed him. He cut off Chongyu's head and held it up to the crowd, shouting: "The Prince of Fusha is coming—you will all be wiped out!

sentences.zh: 今重遇已死，何不亟取文進以贖罪！」

translations.literal: Chongyu is already dead—why not hurry to seize Wenjin to atone for your crimes!
translations.idiomatic: Chongyu is dead—why not seize Wenjin at once to redeem yourselves?"

sentences.zh: 眾踴躍從之，遂斬文進，迎吳成義入城，函二首送建州。

translations.literal: (close of speech.) The crowd leaped up and followed him; they then beheaded Wenjin, welcomed Wu Chengyi into the city, and sent the two heads in a box to Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd surged to follow him. They beheaded Wenjin, welcomed Wu Chengyi into the city, and sent both heads in a casket to Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹復大舉入寇，盧龍節度使趙延壽引兵先進。

translations.literal: The Khitan again launched a major invasion; the military governor of Lulong, Zhao Yanshou, led troops in advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan again invaded in force, with Lulong military governor Zhao Yanshou leading the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 契丹前鋒至邢州，順國節度使杜威遣使間道告急。

translations.literal: The Khitan vanguard reached Xingzhou; the military governor of Shunguo, Du Wei, sent a messenger by a secret route to report the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan vanguard reached Xingzhou, and Shunguo military governor Du Wei sent a messenger by a hidden route to report the crisis.

sentences.zh: 帝欲自將拒之，會有疾，命天平節度使張從思、鄴都留守馬全節、護國節度使安審琦會諸道兵屯邢州，武寧節度使趙在禮屯鄴都。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to lead the army in person to resist them, but fell ill; he ordered the military governor of Tianping, Zhang Cong'en, the defender of Yedu Ma Quanjie, and the military governor of Huguo An Shenqi to assemble troops from the various circuits and encamp at Xingzhou, while the military governor of Wuning Zhao Zaili encamped at Yedu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to take the field himself, but fell ill. He ordered Tianping military governor Zhang Cong'en, Yedu defender Ma Quanjie, and Huguo military governor An Shenqi to gather forces from the circuits and camp at Xingzhou, while Wuning military governor Zhao Zaili held Yedu.

sentences.zh: 契丹主以大兵繼至，建牙於元氏。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler followed with the main army and raised his headquarters at Yuanshi.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler followed with the main host and pitched his headquarters at Yuanshi.

sentences.zh: 朝廷憚契丹之盛，詔從恩等引兵稍卻，於是諸軍恟懼，無復部伍，委棄器甲，所過焚掠，比至相州，不復能整。

translations.literal: The court feared the Khitan's strength and ordered Cong'en and the others to draw their troops back slightly; thereupon the armies panicked, lost all formation, abandoned weapons and armor, and burned and plundered wherever they passed; by the time they reached Xiangzhou they could no longer be re-formed.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Khitan strength, the court ordered Cong'en and the others to pull back slightly. The armies panicked, broke formation, cast away arms and armor, and burned and looted along the march; by the time they reached Xiangzhou they could no longer be brought back into order.

sentences.zh: 齊王中開運二年（

translations.literal: Kaiyun 2 of Later Jin (
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyun 2 of Later Jin (

sentences.zh: 乙巳，公元九四五年）

translations.literal: yisi, the year 945 CE)
translations.idiomatic: yisi, AD 945)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，詔趙在禮還屯澶州，馬全節還鄴都；

translations.literal: Spring, first month: an edict ordered Zhao Zaili to return and encamp at Dazhou, and Ma Quanjie to return to Yedu;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, an edict ordered Zhao Zaili back to Dazhou and Ma Quanjie back to Yedu;

sentences.zh: 又遣右神武統軍張彥澤屯黎陽，西京留守景延廣自滑州引兵守胡梁渡。

translations.literal: also sent the commander of the Right Divine Martial Army Zhang Yanzhe to encamp at Liyang, and the defender of the Western Capital Jing Yanguang to lead troops from Huazhou to guard Huliang Ford.
translations.idiomatic: it also sent Right Divine Martial Army commander Zhang Yanzhe to camp at Liyang and Western Capital defender Jing Yanguang to bring troops from Huazhou to hold Huliang Ford.

sentences.zh: 庚子，張從恩奏契丹逼邢州，詔滑州，鄴都復進軍拒之。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Zhang Cong'en memorialized that the Khitan were pressing Xingzhou; an edict ordered Huazhou and Yedu to advance again with troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi (day 37), Zhang Cong'en reported that the Khitan were pressing Xingzhou; the court ordered forces from Huazhou and Yedu to advance again and resist.

sentences.zh: 義成節度使皇甫遇將兵趣邢州。

translations.literal: The military governor of Yicheng, Huangfu Yu, led troops toward Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng military governor Huangfu Yu marched toward Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇邢、洺、磁三州，殺掠殆盡，入鄴都境。

translations.literal: The Khitan raided the three prefectures Xing, Ming, and Ci, killing and plundering almost to extinction, and entered the territory of Yedu.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ravaged Xing, Ming, and Ci, slaughtering and looting until little remained, then crossed into Yedu's territory.

sentences.zh: 壬子，張從恩、馬全節、安審琦悉以行營兵數萬，陳於相州安陽水之南。

translations.literal: On renzi, Zhang Cong'en, Ma Quanjie, and An Shenqi all arrayed several tens of thousands of campaign troops south of the Anyang River at Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi (day 49), Zhang Cong'en, Ma Quanjie, and An Shenqi drew up tens of thousands of campaign troops south of the Anyang River at Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 皇甫遇與濮州刺史慕容彥超將數千騎前覘契丹，至鄴縣，將渡漳水，遇契丹數萬，遇等且戰且卻。

translations.literal: Huangfu Yu and the prefect of Pu Zhou Murong Yanchao led several thousand horsemen forward to reconnoiter the Khitan; they reached Ye County and were about to cross the Zhang River when they met tens of thousands of Khitan; Yu and the others fought while retreating.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Yu and Pu prefect Murong Yanchao led several thousand cavalry ahead to scout the Khitan. At Ye County, as they were about to ford the Zhang River, they met tens of thousands of Khitan and fought while falling back.

sentences.zh: 至榆林店，契丹大至，二將謀曰：「吾屬今走，死無遺矣！」

translations.literal: At Yulin Inn the Khitan came up in great force; the two generals said: "If we flee now, none of us will survive!
translations.idiomatic: At Yulin post station the Khitan closed in. The two generals said: "If we run now, not one of us will get out alive!"

sentences.zh: 乃止，布陳，自午至未，力戰百餘合，相殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: (close of speech.) They then halted, drew up formation, and from the hour wu to the hour wei fought more than a hundred engagements; casualties on both sides were very heavy.
translations.idiomatic: They halted and drew up formation. From noon to mid-afternoon they fought more than a hundred clashes, with heavy losses on both sides.

sentences.zh: 遇馬斃，因步戰；

translations.literal: Yu's horse was killed, so he fought on foot;
translations.idiomatic: Yu's horse was killed, so he fought on foot;

sentences.zh: 其僕杜知敏以所乘馬授之，遇乘馬復戰。

translations.literal: his servant Du Zhimin gave him the horse he was riding, and Yu mounted and fought again.
translations.idiomatic: his groom Du Zhimin gave Yu his own mount, and Yu remounted and returned to the fight.

sentences.zh: 久之，稍解；

translations.literal: After a long while the fighting eased slightly;
translations.idiomatic: After a long while the fighting eased somewhat;

sentences.zh: 顧知敏已為契丹所擒，遇曰：「知敏義士，不可棄也。」

translations.literal: he saw that Zhimin had already been captured by the Khitan, and Yu said: "Zhimin is a man of righteousness—we cannot abandon him.
translations.idiomatic: he saw that Zhimin had already been taken by the Khitan. Yu said: "Zhimin is a man of honor—we cannot leave him."

sentences.zh: 與彥超躍馬入契丹陳，取知敏而還。

translations.literal: (close of speech.) He and Yanchao spurred their horses into the Khitan formation, seized Zhimin, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yanchao charged into the Khitan lines, pulled Zhimin out, and rode back.

sentences.zh: 俄而契丹繼出新兵來戰。

translations.literal: Before long the Khitan sent fresh troops to fight again.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Khitan brought up fresh troops and attacked again.

sentences.zh: 二將曰：「吾屬勢不可走，以死報國耳。」

translations.literal: The two generals said: "Our position will not let us flee; we can only die in service to the state.
translations.idiomatic: The two generals said: "We cannot break away—we can only die for the realm."

sentences.zh: 日且幕，安陽諸將怪覘兵不還，安審琦曰：「皇甫太師寂無聲問，必為虜所困。」

translations.literal: (close of speech.) As the day neared dusk, the generals at Anyang wondered why the scouts had not returned; An Shenqi said: "Grand Mentor Huangfu is utterly silent—he must be trapped by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: As dusk approached, the generals at Anyang wondered why the scouts had not returned. An Shenqi said: "Grand Mentor Huangfu has gone completely quiet—he must be surrounded."

sentences.zh: 語未卒，有一騎白遇等為虜數萬所圍；

translations.literal: (close of speech.) Before he had finished speaking, a rider reported that Yu and the others were surrounded by tens of thousands of the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: He had barely finished when a rider reported that Yu and his party were encircled by tens of thousands of the enemy;

sentences.zh: 審琦即引騎兵出，將救之，張從恩曰：「此言未足信。

translations.literal: Shenqi at once led cavalry out to rescue them; Zhang Cong'en said: "This report is not enough to trust.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi at once led cavalry out to save them. Zhang Cong'en said: "That report is not reliable enough.

sentences.zh: 必若虜眾猥至，盡吾軍，恐未足以當之，公往何益！」

translations.literal: If the enemy truly come in such overwhelming numbers and we commit our whole army, I fear it still may not be enough to hold them—what good is your going!
translations.idiomatic: If the foe really comes in such numbers and we throw in our entire force, I fear it may still not be enough—what good will your going do?"

sentences.zh: 審琦曰：「成敗，天也。

translations.literal: (close of speech.) Shenqi said: "Success or failure is Heaven's matter.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi said: "Success or failure is Heaven's affair.

sentences.zh: 萬一不濟，當共受之。

translations.literal: If in the end it does not succeed, we should bear it together.
translations.idiomatic: If it fails in the end, we should share the outcome together.

sentences.zh: 借使虜不南來，坐失皇甫太師，吾屬何顏以見天下！」

translations.literal: Even if the enemy do not come south, if we sit by and lose Grand Mentor Huangfu, with what face can we meet the world!
translations.idiomatic: Even if the Khitan never march south, if we sit here and lose Grand Mentor Huangfu, how can we face the empire?"

sentences.zh: 遂逾水而進。

translations.literal: (close of speech.) He then crossed the water and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: He then crossed the river and pressed forward.

sentences.zh: 契丹望見塵起，即解去。

translations.literal: The Khitan, seeing the dust rise, at once dispersed and left.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan saw the dust of his approach and at once broke off and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遇等乃得還，與諸將俱歸相州，軍中皆服二將之勇。

translations.literal: Yu and the others were then able to return; together with the other generals they went back to Xiangzhou, and throughout the army both generals' courage was admired.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and his men were able to get back. They rejoined the other generals at Xiangzhou, and the whole army admired the two men's valor.

sentences.zh: 彥超本吐谷渾也，與劉知遠同母。

translations.literal: Yanchao was originally of the Tuyuhun and shared a mother with Liu Zhiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao was originally Tuyuhun and shared a mother with Liu Zhiyuan.

sentences.zh: 契丹亦引軍退，其眾自相驚曰：「晉軍悉至矣！」

translations.literal: The Khitan also drew their army back; among themselves their troops were alarmed, saying: "All the Jin armies have arrived!
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan also pulled their army back. Their men panicked among themselves, crying: "The whole Jin army is here!"

sentences.zh: 時契丹主在邯鄲，聞之，即時北遁，不再宿，至鼓城。

translations.literal: (close of speech.) At that time the Khitan ruler was at Handan; when he heard it, he fled north at once, staying no second night, and reached Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler was then at Handan. On hearing this he fled north at once, not stopping a second night, and reached Gucheng.

sentences.zh: 是夕，張從恩等議曰：「契丹傾國而來，吾兵不多，城中糧不支一旬，萬一有奸人往告吾虛實，虜悉眾圍我，死無日矣。

translations.literal: That evening Zhang Cong'en and the others deliberated: "The Khitan have come with the whole nation; our troops are few, and the grain in the city will not last ten days. If by chance a traitor goes and tells them our true strength, the enemy will surround us with all their forces and we will have no day left to live.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhang Cong'en and the others debated: "The Khitan have brought the whole nation against us. Our force is small and the city's grain will not last ten days. If some traitor reports our real strength, the foe will surround us with their full host and we will not live to see another day.

sentences.zh: 不若引軍就黎陽倉，南倚大河以拒之，可以萬全。」

translations.literal: Better to lead the army to the Liyang granary and, leaning on the great river to the south to resist them, we can be wholly secure.
translations.idiomatic: Better to march to the Liyang granary and, with the great river at our backs to the south, hold them off—we can be completely safe."

sentences.zh: 議未決，從恩引兵先發，諸軍繼之；

translations.literal: (close of speech.) While the deliberation was not yet settled, Cong'en led the army away first and the other armies followed;
translations.idiomatic: Before the debate was settled, Cong'en marched out first and the other armies followed;

sentences.zh: 擾亂失亡，復如發邢州之時。
