translations.literal: in the turmoil men were lost, just as when they had set out from Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: in the chaos men were lost, just as when they had left Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 從恩等留步兵五百守安陽橋，夜四鼓，知相州事符彥倫謂將佐曰：「此夕紛紜，人無固志，五百弊卒，安能守橋！」

translations.literal: Cong'en and the others left five hundred foot soldiers to guard Anyang Bridge; at the fourth watch of the night Fu Yanlun, who knew affairs at Xiangzhou, said to his officers: "Tonight there is turmoil and no man has a firm will—how can five hundred worn-out soldiers hold the bridge!
translations.idiomatic: Cong'en and the others left five hundred foot soldiers to guard Anyang Bridge. At the fourth watch Fu Yanlun, who was in charge at Xiangzhou, told his officers: "Tonight everything is in uproar and no one has a firm mind—how can five hundred spent troops hold the bridge?"

sentences.zh: 即召入，乘城為備。

translations.literal: (close of speech.) He at once summoned them in and manned the wall to make preparations.
translations.idiomatic: He at once called them in and took the wall to prepare defenses.

sentences.zh: 至曙，望之，契丹數萬騎已陳於安陽水北，彥倫命城上揚旌鼓噪約束，契丹不測。

translations.literal: At dawn, looking out, tens of thousands of Khitan horsemen were already arrayed north of the Anyang River; Yanlun ordered the men on the wall to raise banners, beat drums, shout, and keep discipline; the Khitan could not fathom them.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he looked out and saw tens of thousands of Khitan cavalry already drawn up north of the Anyang River. Yanlun ordered the men on the wall to raise banners, beat drums, shout orders, and keep ranks tight; the Khitan could not read their strength.

sentences.zh: 日加辰，趙延壽與契丹惕隱帥眾逾水，環相州而南，詔右神武統軍張彥澤將兵趣相州。

translations.literal: As the day reached the hour chen, Zhao Yanshou and the Khitan tiyin led their masses across the water, circled Xiangzhou to the south, and an edict ordered the commander of the Right Divine Martial Army Zhang Yanzhe to lead troops toward Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By mid-morning Zhao Yanshou and the Khitan tiyin led their host across the river, swung south around Xiangzhou, and the court ordered Right Divine Martial Army commander Zhang Yanzhe to march toward Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 延壽等至湯陰，聞之，甲寅，引還；

translations.literal: When Yanshou and the others reached Tangyin and heard of it, on jiayin they turned back;
translations.idiomatic: When Yanshou reached Tangyin and heard the news, on jiayin (day 51) he turned back;

sentences.zh: 馬全節等擁大軍在黎陽，不敢追。

translations.literal: Ma Quanjie and the others had the great army at Liyang but did not dare pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Quanjie and the others held the main force at Liyang but did not dare pursue.

sentences.zh: 延壽悉陳甲騎於相州城下，若將攻城狀，符彥倫曰：「此虜將走耳。」

translations.literal: Yanshou fully displayed armored horsemen below the walls of Xiangzhou as if about to attack the city; Fu Yanlun said: "These barbarians are about to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou paraded armored cavalry below Xiangzhou as if to storm the city. Fu Yanlun said: "These barbarians are about to run."

sentences.zh: 出甲卒五百，陳於城北以待之；

translations.literal: (close of speech.) He sent out five hundred armored soldiers and arrayed them north of the city to await them;
translations.idiomatic: He sent out five hundred armored troops and formed them north of the city to meet them;

sentences.zh: 契丹果引去。

translations.literal: the Khitan indeed withdrew and left.
translations.idiomatic: the Khitan did withdraw and leave.

sentences.zh: 以天平節度使張從恩權東京留守。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong'en, military governor of Tianping, was appointed acting defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tianping military governor Zhang Cong'en was made acting defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 庚申，振武節度使折從遠擊契丹，圍勝州，遂攻朔州。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Zhe Congyuan, military governor of Zhenwu, attacked the Khitan, besieged Shengzhou, and then attacked Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen (day 57), Zhenwu military governor Zhe Congyuan struck the Khitan, besieged Shengzhou, then attacked Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 帝疾小愈，河北相繼告急。

translations.literal: The emperor's illness improved slightly, and north of the Yellow River urgent reports came in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's illness eased somewhat, and urgent reports from Hebei kept arriving.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此非安寢之時。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is no time to rest in peace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "This is no time to sleep in peace."

sentences.zh: 乃部分諸將為行計。

translations.literal: (close of speech.) He then assigned the various generals and made plans for the march.
translations.idiomatic: He then assigned the generals and laid plans for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 更命武定軍曰天威軍。

translations.literal: The Wuding Army was renamed the Tianwei Army.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuding Army was renamed the Tianwei Army.

sentences.zh: 北面副招討使馬全節等奏：「據降者言，虜眾不多，宜乘其散歸種落，大舉徑襲幽州。」

translations.literal: Ma Quanjie and the others, deputy commanders for northern recruitment, memorialized: "According to those who surrendered, the enemy force is not large; we should take advantage of their scattering back to their tribes and launch a major strike straight at Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Northern deputy campaign commander Ma Quanjie and others reported: "Surrenders say the enemy host is not large. We should strike while they are dispersing to their tribes and march in force straight on Youzhou."

sentences.zh: 帝以為然，徵兵諸道。

translations.literal: (close of speech.) The emperor thought it right and summoned troops from the various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and called up troops from the circuits.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，下詔親征；

translations.literal: On renxu, an edict announced that he would lead the campaign in person;
translations.idiomatic: On renxu (day 59), an edict announced his personal campaign;

sentences.zh: 乙丑，帝發大梁。

translations.literal: on yichou, the emperor set out from Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: on yichou (day 62) the emperor left Daliang.

sentences.zh: 閩之故臣共迎殷主延政，請歸福州，改國號曰閩。

translations.literal: The former ministers of Min together welcomed the Yin ruler Yanzheng, asked him to return to Fuzhou, and changed the state name to Min.
translations.idiomatic: Min's former ministers together welcomed Yin ruler Yanzheng, asked him to return to Fuzhou, and restored the state name to Min.

sentences.zh: 延政以方有唐兵，未暇徙都，以從子門下侍郎、同平章事繼昌都督南都內外諸軍事，鎮福州；

translations.literal: Yanzheng, because Tang troops were then present, had no leisure to move the capital; he appointed his nephew, Vice Director of the Secretariat and fellow chief councilor Jichang, Grand Commander of the Southern Capital's internal and external military affairs, to garrison Fuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: With Tang forces active, Yanzheng had no time to move the capital. He made his nephew, Secretariat vice director and fellow chief councilor Jichang, overall commander of military affairs inside and outside the Southern Capital, to hold Fuzhou;

sentences.zh: 以飛捷指揮使黃仁諷為鎮遏使，將後衛之。

translations.literal: he appointed the Swift Courier commander Huang Renfeng military suppression commissioner to lead the rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: he appointed Swift Courier commander Huang Renfeng suppression commissioner to command the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 林仁翰至福州，閩主賞之甚薄。

translations.literal: When Lin Renhan reached Fuzhou, the Min ruler rewarded him very meagerly.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Renhan reached Fuzhou, the Min ruler rewarded him very thinly.

sentences.zh: 仁翰未嘗自言其功。

translations.literal: Renhan never spoke of his own merit himself.
translations.idiomatic: Renhan never once spoke of his own deeds.

sentences.zh: 發南都侍衛及兩軍甲士萬五千人，詣建州以拒唐。

translations.literal: He mobilized the Southern Capital guard and fifteen thousand armored men of the two armies and went to Jianzhou to resist Tang.
translations.idiomatic: He mobilized the Southern Capital guard and fifteen thousand armored troops from the two armies and marched to Jianzhou to resist Tang.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬辰朔，帝至滑州，壬申，命安審琦屯鄴都。

translations.literal: Second month, on renchen the new moon, the emperor reached Huazhou; on renshen he ordered An Shenqi to encamp at Yedu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renchen (day 29) the new moon, the emperor reached Huazhou; on renshen (day 9) he ordered An Shenqi to camp at Yedu.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，帝發滑州；

translations.literal: On jiaxu the emperor set out from Huazhou;
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu (day 11) the emperor left Huazhou;

sentences.zh: 乙亥，至澶州。

translations.literal: on yihai he reached Dazhou.
translations.idiomatic: on yihai (day 12) he reached Dazhou.

sentences.zh: 己卯，馬全節等諸軍以次北上。

translations.literal: On jimao the various armies under Ma Quanjie and the others moved north in turn.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao (day 16) the armies under Ma Quanjie and the others advanced north in sequence.

sentences.zh: 劉知遠聞之曰：「中國疲弊，自守恐不足，乃橫挑強胡，勝之猶有後患，況不勝乎！」

translations.literal: When Liu Zhiyuan heard of it he said: "China is worn and exhausted; even to hold what we have may not suffice, yet we go and provoke the strong Hu—if we win there will still be trouble afterward, how much more if we do not win!"
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhiyuan heard this he said: "China is exhausted. Merely holding our own may not be enough, yet we go and provoke the mighty Hu. Even victory will leave trouble behind—what if we lose?"

sentences.zh: 契丹自恆州還，以羸兵驅牛羊過祁州城下，刺史下邳沈斌出兵擊之；

translations.literal: The Khitan returned from Hengzhou and drove lean troops and cattle and sheep past below the walls of Qizhou; the prefect of Xiapi Shen Bin led troops out to attack them;
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan withdrew from Hengzhou and drove weak troops and herds of cattle and sheep past Qizhou. Xiapi prefect Shen Bin led troops out to attack;

sentences.zh: 契丹以精騎奪其城門，州兵不得還。

translations.literal: the Khitan with picked cavalry seized the city gates, and the prefectural troops could not return.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan picked cavalry seized the gates, and the prefectural force could not get back in.

sentences.zh: 趙延壽知城中無餘兵，引契丹急攻之；

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou knew that within the city there were no remaining troops and led the Khitan in a rapid assault;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou, knowing no troops remained in the city, led the Khitan in a swift assault;

sentences.zh: 斌在城上，延壽語之曰：「沈使君，吾之故人，『擇禍莫若輕』，何不早降！」

translations.literal: Bin was on the wall; Yanshou said to him: "Prefect Shen, you are an old friend of mine—'when choosing disaster, none is lighter than the light'—why not surrender early!
translations.idiomatic: Bin was on the wall. Yanshou called to him: "Prefect Shen, you are an old friend of mine—'when you must choose a calamity, take the lightest'—why not surrender now?"

sentences.zh: 斌曰：「侍中父子失計陷身虜庭，忍帥犬羊以殘父母之邦；

translations.literal: (close of speech.) Bin said: "Your Excellency, father and son through mistaken plans fell into the barbarian court, yet you can bear to lead dogs and sheep to ravage the land of your fathers and mothers;
translations.idiomatic: Bin said: "Your Excellency, you and your father through bad counsel fell into the barbarian court, yet you can bear to lead dogs and sheep to ravage the land of your fathers and mothers;

sentences.zh: 不自愧恥，更有驕色，何哉！

translations.literal: you feel no shame for yourself, yet show all the more arrogance—how is that!
translations.idiomatic: you feel no shame, and show only more arrogance—how can that be?

sentences.zh: 沈斌弓折矢盡，寧為國家死耳，終不效公所為！」

translations.literal: Shen Bin's bow is broken and his arrows spent; he would rather die for the state—he will never follow your example!
translations.idiomatic: Shen Bin's bow is broken and his arrows are gone. I would rather die for the state than ever do as you have done!"

sentences.zh: 明日，城陷，斌自殺。

translations.literal: (close of speech.) The next day the city fell and Bin killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the city fell and Bin took his own life.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，詔北面行營都招討使杜威以本道兵會馬全節等進軍。

translations.literal: On bingxu, an edict ordered Du Wei, supreme commander of the northern campaign army, to join his circuit's troops with Ma Quanjie and the others and advance.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu (day 23) an edict ordered northern supreme campaign commander Du Wei to unite his circuit's troops with Ma Quanjie and the others and advance.

sentences.zh: 端明殿學士、戶部侍郎馮玉，宣徽北院使、權侍衛馬步都虞候太原李彥韜，皆挾恩用事，惡中書令桑維翰，數毀之。

translations.literal: Duanming Hall academician and Vice Minister of Revenue Feng Yu, and Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and acting commander of the palace guard horse and foot forces Li Yantao of Taiyuan, both relied on favor to handle affairs, hated the chief councilor Sang Weihan, and repeatedly slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Duanming academician and vice minister of revenue Feng Yu, and northern bureau commissioner and acting commander of the palace horse and foot guard Li Yantao of Taiyuan, both traded on imperial favor, hated chief councilor Sang Weihan, and slandered him again and again.

sentences.zh: 帝欲罷維翰政事，李崧、劉昫固諫而止。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to remove Weihan from government affairs; Li Song and Liu Xu firmly remonstrated and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to strip Weihan of office; Li Song and Liu Xu remonstrated firmly and stopped him.

sentences.zh: 維翰知之，請以玉為樞密副使，玉殊不平。

translations.literal: Weihan learned of it and requested that Yu be made deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Yu was extremely displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan learned of this and asked that Yu be made deputy military affairs commissioner; Yu was deeply resentful.

sentences.zh: 丙申，中旨以玉為戶部尚書、樞密使，以分維翰之權。

translations.literal: On bingshen, an order from the center made Yu Minister of Revenue and military affairs commissioner, to divide Weihan's power.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen (day 33) a central order made Yu minister of revenue and military affairs commissioner, to split Weihan's authority.

sentences.zh: 彥韜少事閻寶，為僕夫，後隸高祖帳下。

translations.literal: Yantao in his youth had served Yan Bao as a groom, and later entered the High Ancestor's personal following.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yantao had served Yan Bao as a groom and later entered the High Ancestor's personal following.

sentences.zh: 高祖自太原南下，留彥韜侍帝，為腹心，由是有寵。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor marched south from Taiyuan he left Yantao to attend the emperor as a trusted intimate, and thereby gained favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor marched south from Taiyuan he left Yantao to attend the emperor as a trusted man, and so won favor.

sentences.zh: 性纖巧，與嬖倖相結，以蔽帝耳目，帝委信之，至於升黜將相，亦得預議。

translations.literal: By nature he was fine and crafty; he joined with the emperor's favorites to block the emperor's eyes and ears; the emperor entrusted him, even to the promotion and dismissal of generals and chief ministers he could take part in discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Crafty by nature, he bonded with the emperor's favorites to screen the emperor's eyes and ears. The emperor relied on him even for promoting and dismissing generals and chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 常謂人曰：「吾不知朝廷設文官何所用，且欲澄汰，徐當盡去之。」

translations.literal: He often said to people: "I do not know what use the court finds in setting up civil officials; I wish to clarify and purge them—in time they will all be removed."
translations.idiomatic: He often told others: "I do not see what use the court has for civil officials. I mean to purge them—in time they will all be gone."

sentences.zh: 唐查文徽表求益兵，唐主以天威都虞候何敬洙為建州行營招討馬步都指揮使，將軍祖全恩為應援使，姚鳳為都監，將兵數千會攻建州，自崇安進屯赤嶺。

translations.literal: Tang Zha Wenhu memorialized requesting additional troops. The Tang ruler appointed He Jingshu, deputy commander of Tianwei, as commander-in-chief of horse and foot for the Jianzhou campaign; General Zu Quan'en as relief commissioner; Yao Feng as overseer; and led several thousand troops to join the attack on Jianzhou, advancing from Chong'an and encamping at Chiling.
translations.idiomatic: Zha Wenhu of Tang submitted a memorial asking for reinforcements. The Tang sovereign made He Jingshu of the Tianwei command post commander-in-chief of the Jianzhou field army for horse and foot; appointed General Zu Quan'en relief commissioner and Yao Feng superintendent; and sent several thousand men to converge on Jianzhou, marching from Chong'an to camp at Chiling.

sentences.zh: 閩主延政遣僕射楊思恭、統軍使陳望將兵萬人拒之，列柵水南，旬餘不戰，唐人不敢逼。

translations.literal: The Min ruler Yan Zheng sent Grand Secretary Yang Sigong and Commander Chen Wang with ten thousand troops to resist them. They set palisades south of the water and for more than ten days did not give battle; the Tang men did not dare press them.
translations.idiomatic: Min ruler Yan Zheng dispatched Grand Secretary Yang Sigong and army commander Chen Wang with ten thousand soldiers to oppose them. They lined stockades on the south bank of the river and for over ten days refused battle, and the Tang troops did not dare close in.

sentences.zh: 思恭以延政之命督望戰。

translations.literal: Sigong, by Yan Zheng's order, urged Wang to fight.
translations.idiomatic: On Yan Zheng's command, Sigong pressed Wang to give battle.

sentences.zh: 望曰：「江、淮兵精，其將習武事。

translations.literal: Wang said: "The soldiers of the Jianghuai are elite, and their generals are versed in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wang said, "The Jianghuai troops are crack soldiers, and their commanders are trained in war.

sentences.zh: 國之安危，系此一舉，不可不萬全而後動。」

translations.literal: The safety of the state hangs on this one move; we must not act until everything is secure.
translations.idiomatic: The realm's survival depends on this single stroke—we cannot move until every precaution is in place."

sentences.zh: 思恭怒曰：「唐兵深侵，陛下寢不交睫，委之將軍。

translations.literal: Sigong said angrily, "The Tang army has invaded deep; His Majesty cannot close his eyes in sleep and has entrusted this to you, General.
translations.idiomatic: Sigong burst out in anger: "The Tang have driven deep into our land. The sovereign cannot so much as close his eyes in sleep, yet he has entrusted everything to you, General.

sentences.zh: 今唐兵不出數千，將軍擁眾萬餘，不乘其未定而擊之，有如唐兵懼而自退，將軍何面目見陛下乎！」

translations.literal: Now the Tang army numbers only a few thousand, while you command more than ten thousand; if you do not strike while they are still unsettled, and the Tang should retreat in fear, with what face will you appear before His Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: The Tang field no more than a few thousand men, while you hold well over ten thousand. If you fail to hit them before they steady themselves, and they should withdraw out of fear—what countenance will you wear when you stand before His Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 望不得已，引兵涉水與唐戰。

translations.literal: Wang had no choice but to lead his army across the water and fight the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang could do nothing else; he led his troops across the river and engaged the Tang.

sentences.zh: 全恩等以大兵當其前，使奇兵出其後，大破之。

translations.literal: Quan'en and the others met them with the main force in front and sent an ambush from behind, routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Quan'en and his colleagues blocked them with the main body in front and sent a flanking force from behind, shattering them completely.

sentences.zh: 望死，思恭僅以身免。

translations.literal: Wang died; Sigong barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Wang was killed; Sigong barely escaped with his own skin.

sentences.zh: 延政大懼，嬰城自守，召董思安、王忠順，使將泉州兵五千詣建州，分守要害。

translations.literal: Yan Zheng was greatly afraid, closed the city and held it, summoned Dong Si'an and Wang Zhongshun, and had them lead five thousand Quanzhou troops to Jianzhou to guard key points separately.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zheng was terrified. He shut himself in the city, called Dong Si'an and Wang Zhongshun, and ordered them to lead five thousand Quanzhou troops to Jianzhou to hold the critical passes.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖置德清軍於故澶州城，乃契丹入寇，澶州、鄴都之間，城戍俱陷。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gaozu had established Deqing Army at the old Chanzou city; when the Khitan invaded, the fortified towns between Chanzou and Yedu all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Gaozu had posted the Deqing Army in the old Chanzou citadel. When the Khitan raided in, every walled post between Chanzou and Yedu was lost.

sentences.zh: 議者以澶州、鄴都相去五十里，宜於中塗築城以應接南北，從之。

translations.literal: Advisors said Chanzou and Yedu were fifty li apart and a city should be built midway to link north and south; the proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors argued that Chanzou and Yedu lay fifty li apart and that a town should be raised halfway between to connect north and south; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊戌，更築德清軍城，合德清、南樂之民以實之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on wuxu day, Deqing Army city was rebuilt anew, and the people of Deqing and Nanle were gathered to populate it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuxu day, the Deqing Army fortress was rebuilt, and the populace of Deqing and Nanle were combined to fill it.

sentences.zh: 初，光州人李仁達，仕閩為元從指揮使，十五年不遷職。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Rendao of Guangzhou had served Min as an "original follower" commander and had not been promoted for fifteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Rendao of Guangzhou had served Min as a commander of the original retinue and had gone fifteen years without promotion.

sentences.zh: 閩主曦之世，叛奔建州，閩主延政以為將。

translations.literal: Under Min ruler Xi he rebelled and fled to Jianzhou; Min ruler Yan Zheng made him a general.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Min ruler Xi he rebelled and fled to Jianzhou; Min ruler Yan Zheng appointed him a general.

sentences.zh: 及朱文進弒曦，復叛奔福州，陳取建州之策。

translations.literal: When Zhu Wenjin assassinated Xi, he again rebelled and fled to Fuzhou, presenting a plan to take Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Wenjin murdered Xi, he rebelled once more, fled to Fuzhou, and offered a plan to seize Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 文進惡其反覆，黜居福清。

translations.literal: Wenjin disliked his fickleness and demoted him to live in Fuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin despised his shifting loyalties and banished him to live in Fuqing.

sentences.zh: 先是浦城人陳繼珣，亦叛閩主延政奔福州，為曦畫策取建州，曦以為著作郎。

translations.literal: Earlier Chen Jixun of Pucheng also rebelled against Yan Zheng and fled to Fuzhou; he had drawn up a plan for Xi to take Jianzhou, and Xi appointed him Gentleman for Authorship.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier still Chen Jixun of Pucheng likewise rebelled against Yan Zheng and fled to Fuzhou. He had devised for Xi the scheme to take Jianzhou, and Xi made him Gentleman for Authorship.

sentences.zh: 及延政得福州，二人皆不自安。

translations.literal: When Yan Zheng took Fuzhou, both men felt ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yan Zheng held Fuzhou, neither man felt secure.

sentences.zh: 王繼昌闇弱嗜酒，不恤將士，將士多怨。

translations.literal: Wang Jichang was dim-witted, fond of wine, and did not care for the troops; the soldiers harbored much resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jichang was dull, weak, and addicted to wine; he showed no concern for the troops, and the soldiers nursed deep grievances.

sentences.zh: 仁達潛入福州，與繼珣說黃仁諷曰：「今唐兵乘勝，建州孤危。

translations.literal: Rendao secretly entered Fuzhou and, with Jixun, persuaded Huang Renfeng, saying: "Now the Tang army is victorious and Jianzhou stands isolated and in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Rendao stole into Fuzhou and, with Jixun, urged Huang Renfeng: "The Tang are riding victory; Jianzhou stands alone and endangered.

sentences.zh: 富沙王不能保建州，安能保福州！

translations.literal: The Prince of Fusha cannot hold Jianzhou—how can he hold Fuzhou!
translations.idiomatic: If the Prince of Fusha cannot keep Jianzhou, how can he keep Fuzhou!

sentences.zh: 昔王潮兄弟，光山布衣耳，取福建如反掌。

translations.literal: In former times the Wang Chao brothers were but plain-cloth men of Guangshan; they took Fujian as easily as turning the hand.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Wang Chao brothers were nothing but hemp-clad commoners of Guangshan, yet they seized Fujian as easily as turning the palm.

sentences.zh: 況吾輩乘此機會，自圖富貴，何患不如彼乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover, if we seize this chance to seek wealth and honor for ourselves, what worry that we may not equal them!
translations.idiomatic: If we seize this moment to carve out fortune for ourselves, what fear that we should fall short of them!"

sentences.zh: 仁諷然之。

translations.literal: Ren Feng agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Feng assented.

sentences.zh: 是夕，仁達等引甲士突入府捨，殺繼昌及吳成義。

translations.literal: That night Rendao and the others led armored men bursting into the government quarters and killed Jichang and Wu Chengyi.
translations.idiomatic: That night Rendao and his party led armored soldiers in a sudden rush into the government compound and killed Jichang and Wu Chengyi.

sentences.zh: 仁達欲自立，恐眾心未服，以雪峰寺僧卓巖明素為眾所重，乃言：「此僧目重瞳子，手垂過膝，真天子也。」

translations.literal: Rendao wished to set himself up as ruler but feared the hearts of the masses were not won; as Zhuo Yanming, a monk of Xuefeng Temple, was esteemed by all, he said: "This monk has double pupils and hands that hang past the knees—he is a true Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Rendao wished to declare himself ruler but feared the crowd was not yet won. Zhuo Yanming, a monk of Xuefeng Temple, had long been respected by all, so he said, "This monk has double pupils and hands that reach below the knee—he is a true Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 相與迎之。

translations.literal: Together they went to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: They went together to bring him in.

sentences.zh: 己亥，立以為帝，解去衲衣，被以袞冕，帥將吏北面拜之。

translations.literal: On jihai day they enthroned him, removed his monastic robes, clothed him in imperial regalia, and led officers and clerks in paying obeisance to the north.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day they raised him as emperor, stripped off his Buddhist robes, arrayed him in imperial vestments, and led officers and clerks in obeisance toward the north.

sentences.zh: 然猶稱天福十年，遣使奉表稱籓於晉。

translations.literal: Yet they still used the reign title Tianfu year ten and sent envoys with a memorial submitting as vassal to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Even so they still dated the year as Tianfu ten and sent envoys with a memorial declaring themselves vassals of Jin.

sentences.zh: 延政聞之，族黃仁諷家，命統軍使張漢真將水軍五千，會漳、泉兵討巖明。

translations.literal: When Yan Zheng heard of it he exterminated Huang Renfeng's clan and ordered Commander Zhang Hanzhen to lead five thousand naval troops, joining Zhang and Quan forces to attack Yanming.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Zheng learned of it he wiped out Huang Renfeng's entire clan and ordered army commander Zhang Hanzhen to take five thousand naval troops, join with Zhangzhou and Quanzhou forces, and march against Yanming.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，杜威等諸軍會於定州，以供奉官蕭處鈞權知祁州事。

translations.literal: On yisi day Du Wei and the various armies assembled at Dingzhou; the attendant-official Xiao Chujun was made acting prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day Du Wei and the allied armies gathered at Dingzhou. The palace attendant Xiao Chujun was appointed acting administrator of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，諸軍攻契丹，泰州刺史晉廷謙舉州降。

translations.literal: On gengxu day the armies attacked the Khitan; Jizhou prefect Jin Tingqian surrendered the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day the armies struck the Khitan. Taizhou prefect Jin Tingqian surrendered the entire prefecture.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，取滿城，獲契丹酋長沒剌及其兵二千人。

translations.literal: On jiayin day they took Mancheng and captured the Khitan chieftain Molà and two thousand of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day they seized Mancheng and took the Khitan chieftain Molà together with two thousand of his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，取遂城。

translations.literal: On yimao day they took Suicheng.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day they took Suicheng.

sentences.zh: 趙延壽部曲有降者言：「契丹主還至虎北口，聞晉取泰州，復擁眾南向，約八萬餘騎，計來夕當至，宜速為備。」

translations.literal: A defector from Zhao Yanshou's following said: "The Khitan ruler has returned to Hubekou; hearing that Jin has taken Taizhou, he has again mustered his forces south—about eighty thousand horsemen—and is expected tonight; prepare quickly.
translations.idiomatic: A man who had deserted from Zhao Yanshou's command reported, "The Khitan ruler withdrew to Hubekou, but on hearing that Jin had taken Taizhou he has massed his host south again—roughly eighty thousand horsemen—and should arrive this very night. Make ready at once."

sentences.zh: 杜威等懼，丙辰，退保泰州。

translations.literal: Du Wei and the others were afraid; on bingchen day they withdrew and defended Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du Wei and his colleagues were alarmed. On bingchen day they fell back to hold Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 戊午，契丹至泰州。

translations.literal: On wuwu day the Khitan reached Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day the Khitan came up to Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 己未，晉軍南行，契丹踵之。

translations.literal: On jiwei day the Jin army marched south and the Khitan followed on their heels.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day the Jin army marched south, the Khitan treading on their heels.

sentences.zh: 晉軍至陽城，庚申，契丹大至。

translations.literal: When the Jin army reached Yangcheng, on gengshen day the Khitan arrived in force.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin reached Yangcheng; on gengshen day the Khitan descended in full strength.

sentences.zh: 晉軍與戰，逐北十餘里，契丹逾白溝而去。

translations.literal: The Jin army fought them and drove them north for more than ten li; the Khitan crossed the Bai Gou and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin gave battle and chased them north more than ten li before the Khitan crossed the White Ditch and pulled away.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，晉軍結陳而南，胡騎四合如山，諸軍力戰拒之。

translations.literal: On renxu day the Jin army formed battle lines and marched south; Khitan horsemen closed in on all four sides like mountains, and the various armies fought desperately to hold them off.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day the Jin army drew up in formation and marched south. Khitan horsemen closed in on every side like moving hills, and every contingent fought with all its strength to beat them back.

sentences.zh: 是日，才行十餘里，人馬饑乏。

translations.literal: That day they had marched only a little more than ten li; men and horses were hungry and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: That day they had covered barely more than ten li; men and horses were starved and spent.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，晉軍至白團衛村，埋鹿角為行寨。

translations.literal: On guihai day the Jin army reached Baituanwei village and buried antler stakes to make a marching camp.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day the Jin army came to Baituanwei village and planted antler palisades for a marching encampment.

sentences.zh: 契丹圍之數重，奇兵出寨後斷糧道。

translations.literal: The Khitan surrounded them in several rings; elite troops emerged behind the camp and cut the supply route.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ringed them in many layers, while picked troops slipped out behind the camp and severed the grain road.

sentences.zh: 是夕，東北風大起，破屋折樹；

translations.literal: That evening a northeast wind rose violently, breaking houses and snapping trees;
translations.idiomatic: That night a northeast gale rose, smashing houses and snapping trees;

sentences.zh: 營中掘井，方及水輒崩，士卒取其泥，帛絞而飲之，人馬俱渴。

translations.literal: In camp they dug wells, but as soon as water was reached the walls collapsed; soldiers took the mud, wrung it through cloth, and drank it—men and horses alike were parched.
translations.idiomatic: within the camp they sank wells, yet the moment water appeared the sides caved in. Soldiers squeezed mud through cloth and drank the drippings; men and horses alike were burning with thirst.

sentences.zh: 至曙，風尤甚。

translations.literal: By dawn the wind grew even fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: By daybreak the wind was worse still.

sentences.zh: 契丹主坐奚車中，令其眾曰：「晉軍止此耳，當盡擒之，然後南取大梁！」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler sat in his Xi cart and ordered his troops: "The Jin army stops here! We shall capture them all, then march south to take Daliang!
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler sat in his cart and told his host, "The Jin army ends here! Take every man, then drive south to seize Daliang!"

sentences.zh: 命鐵鷂四面下馬，拔鹿角而入，奮短兵以擊晉軍，又順風縱火揚塵以助其勢。

translations.literal: He ordered the Iron Hawks on all four sides to dismount, pull up the antler stakes, and enter; they fought with short weapons against the Jin army, and also sent fire and dust downwind to aid their attack.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the Iron Hawks on all four faces to dismount, tear out the antler stakes, and rush in, fighting the Jin with short arms while they loosed fire downwind and raised dust to swell their momentum.

sentences.zh: 軍士皆憤怒，大呼曰：「都招討使何不用兵，令士卒待死！」

translations.literal: The soldiers were all furious and shouted: "Why does the commander-in-chief not use the army and leave the troops to await death!
translations.idiomatic: The troops were enraged and roared, "Why will the commander-in-chief not commit the army and leave the men to wait for death!"

sentences.zh: 諸將請出戰，杜威曰：「俟風稍緩，徐觀可否。」

translations.literal: The generals begged to go out and fight; Du Wei said: "Wait until the wind eases a little, then slowly observe whether it is possible.
translations.idiomatic: The generals pleaded to sally forth. Du Wei said, "Wait until the wind slackens, then watch at leisure whether we can act."

sentences.zh: 馬步都監李守貞曰：「彼眾我寡，風沙之內，莫測多少，惟力鬥者勝，此風乃助我也；

translations.literal: Li Shouzhen, commissioner of horse and foot, said: "They are many and we few; within wind and sand one cannot measure numbers—the side that fights with all its strength wins, and this wind assists us;
translations.idiomatic: Li Shouzhen, overseer of horse and foot, said, "They are many, we few; in wind and blown sand no one can tell the count. Only he who fights with his whole might wins—and this wind is our ally;

sentences.zh: 若俟風止，吾屬無類矣。」

translations.literal: If we wait until the wind stops, none of us will survive.
translations.idiomatic: if we wait for the wind to die, not one of us will be left alive."

sentences.zh: 即呼曰：「諸軍齊擊賊！」

translations.literal: Thereupon he shouted: "All troops, strike the bandits together!
translations.idiomatic: At once he cried, "Every unit—strike the enemy together!"

sentences.zh: 又謂威曰：「令公善守禦，守貞以中軍決死矣！」

translations.literal: He also said to Wei: "Your Excellency defend well; Shouzhen will stake the center army on a fight to the death!
translations.idiomatic: He told Wei further, "Your Excellency hold the defenses; Shouzhen will throw the central army into a battle to the death!"

sentences.zh: 馬軍左廂都排陳使張彥澤召諸將問計，皆曰：「虜得風勢，宜俟風回與戰。」

translations.literal: Zhang Yanze, left wing commander of the horse army, summoned the generals to ask advice; all said: "The barbarians have the wind's favor; we should wait for the wind to shift before fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanze, left-wing commander of the horse army, called the generals to counsel. All said, "The barbarians hold the wind's advantage; we ought to wait until it turns before we fight."

sentences.zh: 彥澤亦以為然。

translations.literal: Yanze also thought so.
translations.idiomatic: Yanze agreed.

sentences.zh: 諸將退，馬軍右廂副排陳使太原藥元福獨留，謂彥澤曰：「今軍中飢渴已甚，若俟風回，吾屬已為虜矣。

translations.literal: When the generals withdrew, the deputy right-wing horse commander from Taiyuan, Yao Yuanfu, alone remained and said to Yanze: "The army is already desperately hungry and thirsty; if we wait for the wind to turn, we will already be captives of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The generals withdrew, but Yao Yuanfu of Taiyuan, deputy right-wing commander of the horse army, stayed behind and told Yanze, "The army is already half dead from hunger and thirst. If we wait for the wind to change, we will already be the enemy's prisoners.

sentences.zh: 敵謂我不能逆風以戰，宜出其不意急擊之，此兵之詭道也。」

translations.literal: The enemy thinks we cannot fight against the wind; we should take them by surprise and strike hard—this is the crafty way of war.
translations.idiomatic: They believe we cannot fight into the wind. Strike them unawares and hard—that is war's deceit."

sentences.zh: 馬步左右廂都排陳使符彥卿曰：「與其束手就擒，曷若以身徇國！」

translations.literal: Fu Yanqing of the left and right wings said: "Rather than sit bound and be taken, how much better to give one's body for the state!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanqing, commander of both horse wings, said, "Better to offer one's body to the state than sit bound and be seized!"

sentences.zh: 乃與彥澤、元福及左廂都排陳使皇甫遇引精騎出西門擊之，諸將繼至。

translations.literal: Then together with Yanze, Yuanfu, and left-wing commander Huangfu Yu they led elite cavalry out the west gate to strike them; the other generals followed.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Yanze, Yuanfu, and left-wing commander Huangfu Yu in leading picked cavalry out the west gate to attack; the other generals came after.

sentences.zh: 契丹卻數百步。

translations.literal: The Khitan fell back several hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan recoiled several hundred paces.

sentences.zh: 彥卿等謂守貞曰：「且曳隊往來乎？

translations.literal: Yanqing and the others said to Shouzhen: "Shall we drag our ranks back and forth for a while?
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing and the rest asked Shouzhen, "Shall we wheel the line to and fro awhile?

sentences.zh: 直前奮擊，以勝為度乎？」

translations.literal: Or press straight ahead and fight desperately, taking victory as the measure?
translations.idiomatic: Or drive straight forward and fight to the limit of victory?"

sentences.zh: 守貞曰：「事勢如此，安可回鞚！

translations.literal: Shouzhen said: "The situation is as it is—how can we turn the bridle!
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen said, "Matters stand as they stand—how can we turn the reins!

sentences.zh: 宜長驅取勝耳！」

translations.literal: We should drive straight ahead and seize the victory!
translations.idiomatic: Press on at full gallop and take the win!"

sentences.zh: 彥卿等躍馬而去，風勢益甚，昏晦如夜，彥卿等擁萬餘騎橫擊契丹，呼聲動天地，契丹大敗而走，勢如崩山。

translations.literal: Yanqing and the others spurred their horses and charged; the wind grew stronger still, dusk dark as night; Yanqing and the others led more than ten thousand horsemen in a transverse strike on the Khitan; their shouts shook heaven and earth; the Khitan were utterly defeated and fled, their momentum like a collapsing mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing and his fellows lashed their horses forward. The wind rose still higher, darkness thick as night. More than ten thousand horsemen under Yanqing swept sideways into the Khitan; their battle cries shook heaven and earth. The Khitan were smashed and fled, their rout like a mountain in collapse.

sentences.zh: 李守貞亦令步兵盡拔鹿角出鬥，步騎俱進，逐北二十餘里。

translations.literal: Li Shouzhen also ordered the foot soldiers to pull up all the antler stakes and come out fighting; foot and horse advanced together, pursuing north more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shouzhen likewise ordered the infantry to uproot every antler stake and pour out to fight. Foot and horse went forward together, chasing the foe north more than twenty li.

sentences.zh: 鐵鷂既下馬，蒼皇不能復上，皆委棄馬及鎧仗蔽地。

translations.literal: The Iron Hawks, having dismounted, could not remount in haste and all abandoned their horses and armor that covered the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The Iron Hawks, already on foot, could not regain their saddles in the panic and cast away horses and armor until the ground was buried under them.

sentences.zh: 契丹散卒至陽城東南水上，稍復布列。

translations.literal: Scattered Khitan troops reached the waters southeast of Yangcheng and gradually re-formed ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Broken Khitan bands reached the waters southeast of Yangcheng and slowly drew up again.

sentences.zh: 杜威曰：「賊已破膽，不宜更令成列！」

translations.literal: Du Wei said: "The bandits' courage is already broken; we must not let them form lines again!
translations.idiomatic: Du Wei said, "The enemy's nerve is already shattered—we must not let them form ranks again!"

sentences.zh: 遣精騎擊之，皆渡水去。

translations.literal: He sent elite cavalry to strike them; all crossed the water and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He sent picked horsemen to hit them, and all forded the water and ran.

sentences.zh: 契丹主乘奚車走十餘里，追兵急，獲一橐駝，乘之而走。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler rode his Xi cart and fled more than ten li; pursuit pressed hard; he obtained a camel and rode it away.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler fled in his cart for more than ten li. Pursuit closed tight, so he seized a Bactrian camel and rode it off.

sentences.zh: 諸將請急追之。

translations.literal: The generals asked to pursue hotly.
translations.idiomatic: The generals begged to press the pursuit hard.

sentences.zh: 杜威揚言曰：「逢賊幸不死，更索衣囊邪？」

translations.literal: Du Wei proclaimed aloud: "We met the bandits and luckily did not die—shall we now demand their baggage as well?
translations.idiomatic: Du Wei announced publicly, "We met the enemy and by luck did not die—must we now go after their baggage too?"

sentences.zh: 李守貞曰：「兩日人馬渴甚，今得水飲之，皆足重，難以追寇，不若全軍而還。」

translations.literal: Li Shouzhen said: "For two days men and horses have been desperately thirsty; now they have found water and drunk it, all are weighted down and we cannot pursue the enemy—better to bring the whole army back.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shouzhen said, "For two days men and horses have been parched beyond bearing. Now they have water and have drunk their fill; every man is heavy on his feet and we cannot run the foe down. Better to bring the whole army home."

sentences.zh: 乃退保定州。

translations.literal: Thereupon they withdrew to Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: They then fell back to Baoding.

sentences.zh: 契丹主至幽州，散兵稍集；

translations.literal: When the Khitan ruler reached Youzhou, scattered troops gradually gathered;
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan ruler reached Youzhou, his scattered soldiers slowly reassembled;

sentences.zh: 以軍失利，杖其酋長各數百，唯趙延壽得免。

translations.literal: Because the army had been defeated, he flogged each chieftain several hundred strokes; only Zhao Yanshou was spared.
translations.idiomatic: because the campaign had failed, he had every chieftain beaten several hundred blows—only Zhao Yanshou was excused.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，諸軍自定州引歸。

translations.literal: On yichou day the various armies withdrew from Dingzhou and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day the allied armies marched back from Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔以泰州隸定州。

translations.literal: An edict made Taizhou subordinate to Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict placed Taizhou under Dingzhou's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛巳，帝發澶州，甲申，還大梁。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, on xinsi day the emperor set out from Chanzou; on jiashen day he returned to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on xinsi day the emperor left Chanzou; on jiashen day he was back in Daliang.

sentences.zh: 己丑，復以鄴都為天雄軍。

translations.literal: On jichou day Yedu was again made Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day Yedu was restored as the Tianxiong command.

sentences.zh: 閩張漢真至福州，攻其東關。

translations.literal: Min Zhang Hanzhen reached Fuzhou and attacked its east gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hanzhen of Min arrived at Fuzhou and assaulted the eastern gate.

sentences.zh: 黃仁諷聞其家夷滅，開門力戰，大破閩兵，執漢真，入城，斬之。

translations.literal: Huang Renfeng heard his family had been annihilated, opened the gate and fought desperately, routed the Min army, seized Hanzhen, brought him into the city, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Renfeng learned that his clan had been exterminated. He threw open the gate, fought with desperate force, routed the Min troops, seized Hanzhen, dragged him into the city, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 卓巖明無它方略，但於殿上噀水散豆，作諸法事而已。

translations.literal: Zhuo Yanming had no other strategy but to spray water and scatter beans in the hall and perform various ritual acts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo Yanming had no policy beyond spitting water and scattering beans in the hall and carrying out ritual observances.

sentences.zh: 又遣使迎其父於莆田，尊為太上皇。

translations.literal: He also sent envoys to welcome his father from Putian and honored him as Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys to bring his father from Putian and exalted him as Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 李仁達既立巖明，自判六軍諸衛事，使黃仁諷屯西門，陳繼珣屯北門。

translations.literal: After Rendao had enthroned Yanming, he himself assumed control of the Six Armies and palace guards, posting Huang Renfeng at the west gate and Chen Jixun at the north gate.
translations.idiomatic: Once Rendao had set Yanming on the throne, he took command of the Six Armies and palace guards himself, stationing Huang Renfeng at the west gate and Chen Jixun at the north gate.

sentences.zh: 仁諷從容謂繼珣曰：「人之所以為人，以有忠、信、仁、義也。

translations.literal: Renfeng said calmly to Jixun: "What makes a man a man is the possession of loyalty, faith, benevolence, and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Renfeng said quietly to Jixun, "A man is a man because he keeps loyalty, faith, benevolence, and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 吾頃嘗有功於富沙，中間叛之，非忠也；

translations.literal: I once had merit under Fusha, then rebelled against him midway—not loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: I once served Fusha with credit, then turned rebel midway—that is not loyalty;

sentences.zh: 人以從子托我而與人殺之，非信也；

translations.literal: A man entrusted his nephew to me and I had him killed by others—not faith;
translations.idiomatic: a man entrusted his nephew to me and I let others kill him—that is not faith;

sentences.zh: 屬者與建兵戰，所殺皆鄉曲故人，非仁也；

translations.literal: Recently in fighting the Jianzhou army, those I killed were all fellow townsmen and old acquaintances—not benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: in the recent war with the Jianzhou troops, everyone I killed was a neighbor or old friend—that is not benevolence;

sentences.zh: 棄妻子，使人魚肉之，非義也。

translations.literal: I abandoned wife and children and let others treat them as fish on the chopping block—not righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: I cast off wife and children and let others carve them like fish on the block—that is not righteousness.

sentences.zh: 此身十沉九浮，死有餘愧！」

translations.literal: This body has sunk nine times in ten and risen once; in death there is surplus shame!
translations.idiomatic: This body has gone under nine times in ten and floated up once—to die still leaves shame enough!"

sentences.zh: 因拊膺慟哭。

translations.literal: Thereupon he beat his breast and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: He clapped his chest and wept in anguish.

sentences.zh: 繼珣曰：「大丈夫徇功名，何顧妻子！

translations.literal: Jixun said: "A great man devotes himself to fame and reputation—why consider wife and children!
translations.idiomatic: Jixun said, "A great man sells himself for fame and rank—why trouble over wife and children!

sentences.zh: 宜置此事，勿以取禍。」

translations.literal: You should put this matter aside and not invite disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Put such thoughts away and do not bring ruin on yourself."

sentences.zh: 仁達聞之，使人告仁諷、繼珣謀反，皆殺之。

translations.literal: When Rendao heard of it, he had someone report that Renfeng and Jixun were plotting rebellion; both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Rendao heard of this, he sent word that Renfeng and Jixun were plotting revolt, and had both of them executed.

sentences.zh: 由是兵權盡歸仁達。

translations.literal: Thereupon military authority entirely returned to Renda.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, all military authority passed to Li Renda.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙申朔，大赦。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day of the cycle (bingchen), a great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the first day of the month (bingchen), the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 順國節度使杜威，久鎮恆州，性貪殘，自恃貴戚，多不法。

translations.literal: Shunguo Military Commissioner Du Wei had long garrisoned Hengzhou; by nature greedy and cruel, relying on his noble kinship, he committed many unlawful acts.
translations.idiomatic: Du Wei, military commissioner of Shunguo, had long held Hengzhou. Greedy and brutal by nature, he leaned on his status as an imperial in-law and broke the law repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 每以備邊為名，斂吏民錢帛以充私藏。

translations.literal: Each time in the name of border defense he levied money and silk from officials and commoners to fill his private hoard.
translations.idiomatic: He regularly extorted cash and cloth from officials and civilians under the pretext of frontier defense, stockpiling it for himself.

sentences.zh: 富室有珍貨或名姝、駿馬，皆虜取之；

translations.literal: When wealthy households had precious goods, celebrated beauties, or fine horses, he seized them all;
translations.idiomatic: If a rich household possessed rare valuables, renowned beauties, or fine steeds, he plundered them outright;

sentences.zh: 或誣以罪殺之，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: or falsely charged them with crimes and killed them, confiscating their households.
translations.idiomatic: or framed them on false charges, had them executed, and confiscated their estates.

sentences.zh: 又畏懦過甚，每契丹數十騎入境，威已閉門登陴；

translations.literal: Moreover he was excessively timid and cowardly; whenever several dozen Khitan horsemen crossed the border, Wei had already shut the gates and mounted the battlements;
translations.idiomatic: He was also abjectly cowardly: at the sight of even a few dozen Khitan horsemen crossing the border, Wei would already have shut the gates and manned the walls;

sentences.zh: 或數騎驅所掠華人千百過城下，威但□真目延頸望之，無意邀取。

translations.literal: or when several horsemen drove hundreds or thousands of captured Chinese past below the walls, Wei would only □ fix his eyes and crane his neck to watch, with no intent to intercept.
translations.idiomatic: or when a handful of riders drove hundreds or thousands of captured Chinese past beneath the walls, Wei would merely glare and crane his neck to watch, with no thought of intercepting them.

sentences.zh: 由是虜無所忌憚，屬城多為所屠，威竟不出一卒救之，千里之間，暴骨如莽，村落殆盡。

translations.literal: Hence the barbarians had nothing to fear; neighboring prefectures were often massacred by them, yet Wei to the end did not send a single soldier to rescue them; for a thousand li, exposed bones piled like scrub, and villages were nearly extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan therefore had nothing to fear from him. Subordinate cities were repeatedly sacked, yet Wei never dispatched a single trooper to their aid; for a thousand li, bleaching bones lay thick as brush, and hamlets were all but wiped from the map.

sentences.zh: 威見所部殘弊，為眾所怨，又畏契丹之強，累表請入朝，帝不許；

translations.literal: Wei, seeing his command ruined and detested by the masses, and fearing Khitan strength, repeatedly memorialized requesting to enter court; the emperor would not permit it;
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his district laid waste and himself loathed by his troops, and fearing Khitan power besides, Wei memorialized again and again to return to court; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 威不俟報，遽委鎮入朝，朝廷聞之，驚駭。

translations.literal: Without awaiting a reply, Wei abruptly abandoned his post and entered court; when the court heard of it, it was stunned and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Without waiting for a response, he abruptly quit his command and came to court. When word reached the capital, the court was stunned.

sentences.zh: 桑維翰言於帝曰：「威固違朝命，擅離邊鎮。

translations.literal: Sang Weinhan said to the emperor: "Wei has indeed defied the court's order and left the frontier command on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Weinhan said to the emperor, "Wei has plainly defied the court by quitting a frontier post without authorization.

sentences.zh: 居常憑恃勳親，邀求姑息，及疆場多事，曾無守禦之意；

translations.literal: In ordinary times he relies on meritorious kinship and demands indulgence; now that the borderlands are in turmoil, he has never had the will to defend and guard;
translations.idiomatic: He habitually trades on his ties to the throne and demands leniency; now that the marches are in crisis, he has shown not the slightest will to hold the line;

sentences.zh: 宜因此時廢之，庶無後患。」

translations.literal: it is fitting to dismiss him at this moment, that there may be no trouble afterward."
translations.idiomatic: the time is right to remove him, lest trouble follow later."

sentences.zh: 帝不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 維翰曰：「陛下不忍廢之，宜授以近京小鎮，勿復委以雄籓。」

translations.literal: Weinhan said: "If Your Majesty cannot bear to dismiss him, he should be given a small command near the capital—do not again entrust him with a great strategic prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Weinhan said, "If Your Majesty cannot bring yourself to dismiss him, grant him a minor post near the capital, and do not again invest him in a powerful frontier command."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「威，朕之密親，必無異志；

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Wei is my close kin; he is sure to harbor no other intent;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Wei is my close kinsman and surely harbors no disloyal intent;

sentences.zh: 但宋國長公主切欲相見耳，公勿以為疑！」

translations.literal: only the Princess of Songlong ardently wishes to see him—that is all. Do not suspect him!"
translations.idiomatic: only the Princess of Songlong longs to see him—that is all. Sir, do not cast doubt on him!"

sentences.zh: 維翰自是不敢復言國事，以足疾辭位。

translations.literal: From then on Weinhan did not dare again to speak of state affairs; citing a foot ailment, he resigned his post.
translations.idiomatic: From then Sang Weinhan dared not raise state affairs again; citing a foot ailment, he resigned his office.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，威至大梁。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Wei arrived at Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Du Wei reached Daliang.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，李仁達大閱戰士，請卓巖明臨視。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Li Renda mustered troops on grand review and invited Zhuo Yanming to attend and observe.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Li Renda reviewed his troops in grand array and invited Zhuo Yanming to attend.

sentences.zh: 仁達陰教軍士突前登階，刺殺巖明。

translations.literal: Renda secretly instructed soldiers to rush forward up the steps and stab Yanming to death.
translations.idiomatic: Renda secretly told his soldiers to surge forward up the steps and stab Yanming to death.

sentences.zh: 仁達陽驚，狼狽而走。

translations.literal: Renda feigned alarm and fled in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: Renda feigned shock and fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 軍士共執仁達，使居巖明之坐。

translations.literal: The soldiers together seized Renda and had him take Yanming's seat.
translations.idiomatic: The troops seized Renda in turn and seated him in Yanming's chair.

sentences.zh: 仁達乃自稱威武留後，用保大年號，奉表稱籓於唐，亦遣使入貢於晉；

translations.literal: Renda then styled himself Acting Weiwu military commissioner, adopted the Baoda reign-era name, submitted a memorial declaring himself Tang's vassal, and also sent envoys to pay tribute to Jin;
translations.idiomatic: Renda then proclaimed himself acting commissioner of Weiwu, adopted Tang's Baoda reign title, sent a memorial pledging vassalage to Tang, and dispatched envoys to pay tribute to Jin as well;

sentences.zh: 並殺巖明之父。

translations.literal: and also killed Yanming's father.
translations.idiomatic: and had Yanming's father put to death.

sentences.zh: 唐以仁達為威武節度使、同平章事，賜名弘義，編之屬籍。

translations.literal: Tang appointed Renda military commissioner of Weiwu, Tongpingzhangshi, granted the name Hongyi, and entered him in the imperial clan register.
translations.idiomatic: Tang appointed him military commissioner of Weiwu and Tongpingzhangshi, granted the name Hongyi, and entered him on the imperial clan rolls.

sentences.zh: 弘義又遣使修好於吳越。

translations.literal: Hongyi also sent envoys to pursue good relations with Wuyue.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyi also sent envoys to open friendly relations with Wuyue.

sentences.zh: 己未，杜威獻部曲步騎合四千人並鎧仗，庚申，又獻粟十萬斛、芻二十萬束，雲皆在本道。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Du Wei presented his personal retinue of four thousand foot and horse together with armor and weapons; on gengshen he also presented one hundred thousand hu of grain and two hundred thousand bundles of fodder, saying all were still in his circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Du Wei presented four thousand infantry and cavalry of his personal command, with armor and weapons; on gengshen he offered one hundred thousand hu of grain and two hundred thousand bundles of fodder, claiming all remained in his circuit.

sentences.zh: 帝以其所獻騎兵隸扈聖，步兵隸護國，威復請以為牙隊，而稟賜皆仰縣官。

translations.literal: The emperor assigned the presented cavalry to the Husheng guard and the infantry to the Huguo guard; Wei again requested they serve as his personal escort, while rations and gifts were supplied from the government granaries.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assigned the cavalry to the Husheng guard corps and the infantry to the Huguo guard corps; Wei asked that they again serve as his personal retainers, with pay and provisions drawn from the state.

sentences.zh: 威又令公主白帝，求天雄節鉞，帝許之。

translations.literal: Wei also had the princess report to the emperor, seeking the seal of Tianxiong military commissioner; the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Through the princess he petitioned for the Tianxiong command; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 唐兵圍建州，屢破泉州兵。

translations.literal: Tang forces besieged Jianzhou and repeatedly defeated Quanzhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: Tang armies besieged Jianzhou and repeatedly routed Quanzhou's forces.

sentences.zh: 許文稹敗唐兵於汀州，執其將時厚卿。

translations.literal: Xu Wenzhen defeated Tang forces at Tingzhou and captured the general Shi Houqing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wenzhen defeated Tang troops at Tingzhou and took their general Shi Houqing prisoner.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸酉，以杜威為天雄節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on guiyou, Du Wei was appointed military commissioner of Tianxiong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guiyou, Du Wei was appointed military commissioner of Tianxiong.

sentences.zh: 契丹連歲入寇，中國疲於奔命，邊民塗地；

translations.literal: The Khitan raided year after year; the Middle Kingdom was exhausted from rushing to respond, and border folk lay slaughtered across the ground;
translations.idiomatic: Year after year the Khitan raided inward; the realm was worn out from emergency marches, and border populations were slaughtered wholesale;

sentences.zh: 契丹人畜亦多死，國人厭苦之。

translations.literal: Khitan people and livestock also died in great numbers, and their countrymen wearied of the suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan people and herds likewise suffered heavy losses, and their people grew sick of the hardship.

sentences.zh: 述律太后謂契丹主曰：「使漢人為胡主，可乎？」

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Shulü said to the Khitan ruler: "To make a Chinese man ruler over the Hu—would that do?"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Shulü said to the Khitan emperor, "Would it do to set a Chinese man as ruler over the Hu?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「不可。」

translations.literal: He said, "It is not possible."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "It cannot be done."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「然則汝何故欲為漢主？」

translations.literal: The empress dowager said, "Then why do you wish to become ruler over the Chinese?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Then why do you wish to become ruler over the Chinese?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「石氏負恩，不可容。」

translations.literal: He said, "The Shi clan has betrayed favor; they cannot be tolerated."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The Shi have betrayed our favor; they cannot be endured."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「汝今雖得漢地，不能居也；

translations.literal: The empress dowager said, "Though you now gain Chinese territory, you cannot dwell in it;
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Though you seize Chinese territory now, you cannot hold it;

sentences.zh: 萬一蹉跌，悔何所及！」

translations.literal: if by any chance you stumble and fall, what regret could make amends!"
translations.idiomatic: should you stumble once, remorse will come too late!"

sentences.zh: 又謂其群下曰：「漢兒何得一向眠！

translations.literal: She also said to her assembled followers: "How can these Chinese brats go on sleeping at ease!
translations.idiomatic: She also told her ministers, "How can these Chinese pups keep sleeping as they please!

sentences.zh: 自古但聞漢和蕃，未聞蕃和漢。

translations.literal: From antiquity one has heard only of Chinese making peace with the frontier peoples, never of the frontier peoples making peace with the Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity one has heard only of Chinese suing the frontier tribes for peace, never of tribes suing the Chinese.

sentences.zh: 漢兒果能回意，我亦何惜與和！」

translations.literal: If the Chinese brats can indeed change their minds, what would I begrudge in making peace!"
translations.idiomatic: If the Chinese truly change their minds, what would I begrudge in granting peace!"

sentences.zh: 桑維翰屢勸帝復請和於契丹以紓國患，帝假開封軍將張暉供奉官，使奉表稱臣詣契丹，卑辭謝過。

translations.literal: Sang Weinhan repeatedly urged the emperor to renew peace requests to the Khitan to ease the state's affliction. The emperor lent the Kaifeng military officer Zhang Hui the title of palace supply officer and had him present a memorial declaring himself subject and go to the Khitan, with humble words apologizing for faults.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Weinhan repeatedly urged the emperor to seek peace with the Khitan again to ease the national crisis. The emperor lent Kaifeng military officer Zhang Hui the rank of palace attendant and sent him with a memorial declaring vassalage to the Khitan, apologizing in abject terms.

sentences.zh: 契丹主曰：「使景延廣、桑維翰自來，仍割鎮、定兩道隸我，則可和。」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler said: "Have Jing Yanguang and Sang Weinhan come in person, and furthermore cede the Zhen and Ding circuits to my jurisdiction—then peace may be made.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor said, "Have Jing Yanguang and Sang Weinhan come in person, and cede the Zhen and Ding circuits to me—then peace may be discussed.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以契丹語忿，謂其無和意，乃止。

translations.literal: The court, because the Khitan words were angry, judged that they had no intent of peace, and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The court took the Khitan reply as wrathful and concluded that no sincere desire for peace existed, and broke off the effort.

sentences.zh: 及契丹主入大梁，謂李崧等曰：「曏使晉使再來，則南北不戰矣。」

translations.literal: When the Khitan ruler later entered Daliang, he said to Li Song and others: "Had Jin envoys come again as before, north and south would not have fought."
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan emperor later entered Daliang, he told Li Song and others, "Had Jin sent envoys once more, north and south would never have fought."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，閩人或告福州援兵謀叛，閩主延政收其鎧仗，遣還，伏兵於隘，盡殺之，死者八千餘人，脯其肉以歸為食。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, a Min man reported that Fuzhou relief troops plotted rebellion; the Min ruler Yanzheng gathered up their armor and weapons, sent them back, set an ambush at the pass, and killed them to the last—more than eight thousand dead; their flesh was cured as provisions to carry home for food.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, some Min men reported that Fuzhou relief troops were plotting rebellion. The Min ruler Yanzheng confiscated their arms, sent them homeward, then ambushed them in a defile and slaughtered them all—more than eight thousand dead. Their flesh was cured and carried back for rations.

sentences.zh: 唐邊鎬拔鐔州，查文徽之黨魏岑、馮延己、延魯以師出有功，皆踴躍贊成之。

translations.literal: Tang's Bian Hao took Tazhou; Cha Wenhui's faction—Wei Cen, Feng Yanji, and Yan Lu—because the expedition's first outing had merit, all leaped up to endorse it.
translations.idiomatic: Tang's Bian Hao captured Tazhou. Wei Cen, Feng Yanji, Yan Lu, and the rest of Cha Wenhui's faction, heartened by the army's early success, all pressed enthusiastically for more.

sentences.zh: 徵求供億，府庫為之耗竭，洪、饒、撫、信之民尤苦之。

translations.literal: Levies for supplies and transports drained the treasuries; the people of Hong, Rao, Fu, and Xin especially suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Requisitions for grain and transport emptied the treasuries; the peoples of Hong, Rao, Fu, and Xin suffered worst of all.

sentences.zh: 延政遣使奉表稱臣於吳越，請為附庸以求救。

translations.literal: Yanzheng sent envoys with a memorial declaring himself subject to Wuyue, requesting to become a subordinate state in order to seek rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzheng sent envoys with a memorial declaring vassalage to Wuyue, asking to become a tributary state in exchange for rescue.

sentences.zh: 楚王希範疑靜江節度使兼侍中、知朗州希杲得人心，遣人伺之。

translations.literal: King of Chu Xi Fan suspected that Military Commissioner of Jingjiang and Palace Attendant, acting prefect of Langzhou Xi Gao had won men's hearts, and sent men to watch him.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Chu, Xi Fan, suspected that Xi Gao, military commissioner of Jingjiang, palace attendant, and administrator of Langzhou, had won the people's loyalty and sent men to watch him.

sentences.zh: 希杲懼，稱疾求歸，不許；

translations.literal: Xi Gao was afraid; he pleaded illness and asked to return, but was not permitted;
translations.idiomatic: Xi Gao grew fearful; he pleaded illness and asked to leave, but permission was refused;

sentences.zh: 遣醫往視疾，因毒殺之。

translations.literal: physicians were sent to examine his illness, and on that pretext he was poisoned to death.
translations.idiomatic: the court sent physicians to examine his illness and poisoned him on the pretext.
